title.zh: 卷五十四 吳書九 周瑜魯肅呂蒙傳
title.en: Volume 54: Book of Wu 9 - Biographies of Zhou Yu, Lu Su, and Lü Meng
title.raw: 卷五十四 吳書九 周瑜魯肅呂蒙傳 Volume 54: Book of Wu 9 - Biographies of Zhou Yu, Lu Su, and Lü Meng

sentences.zh: 周瑜字公瑾，廬江舒人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Yu, courtesy name Gongjin, was a man of Shu in Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu, courtesy Gongjin, came from Shu county in Lujiang commandery.

sentences.zh: 從祖父景，景子忠，皆為漢太尉。

translations.literal: His father’s uncle Jing, and Jing’s son Zhong, both served as Grand Commandant of Han.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather’s cousin Zhou Jing and Jing’s son Zhou Zhong each rose to Han grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 〈謝承《後漢書》曰：景字仲鄉，少以廉能見稱，以明學察孝廉，辟公府。

translations.literal: Xie Cheng’s Later Han shu states: Jing, courtesy Zhongxiang, in youth was praised for integrity and ability, through bright learning was nominated flourishing talent, and was summoned to the high offices.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Cheng’s *Later Han History* records Zhou Jing, courtesy Zhongxiang, famed young for honesty and competence, nominated flourishing talent on scholarly merit, then summoned to the capital ministries.

sentences.zh: 後為豫州刺史，辟汝南陳蕃為別駕，潁川李膺、荀緄、杜密、沛國硃寓為從事，皆天下英俊之士也。

translations.literal: Later he became Inspector of Yu Province, summoned Chen Fan of Runan as chief clerk on the inspector’s staff, and Li Ying, Xun Gun, Du Mi of Yingchuan, and Zhu Yu of Pei as aides—all were outstanding talents of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: As governor of Yu he hired Chen Fan of Runan as chief clerk and Li Ying, Xun Gun, Du Mi, and Zhu Yu as staff advisers—each among the finest men of the age.

sentences.zh: 稍遷至尚書令，遂登太尉。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Director of the Masters of Writing, then ascended to Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed step by step to director of the secretariat and then grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 張璠《漢紀》曰：景父榮，章、和世為尚書令。

translations.literal: Zhang Fan’s Han ji states: Jing’s father Rong was Director of the Masters of Writing in the Zhanghe and Yonghe reigns.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fan’s *Han Annals* adds that Zhou Jing’s father Rong had held the same director’s post under Emperors Zhang and He.

sentences.zh: 初景歷位牧守，好善愛士，每歲舉孝廉，延請入，上後堂，與家人宴會，如此者數四。

translations.literal: At first Jing successively held posts as shepherd and defender; he loved the good and cherished gentlemen; each year he nominated flourishing talent, invited them in, led them to the rear hall, and feasted with his household—thus several times.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jing, while serving as regional inspector and governor, loved nurturing talent: every year he nominated flourishing candidates, brought them to his rear hall, and feasted them with his family—again and again.

sentences.zh: 及贈送既備，又選用其子弟，常稱曰：「移臣作子，於政何有？

translations.literal: When gifts were already complete, he again selected and employed their sons and younger brothers, often saying, “Shift a minister to become a son—what harm is there to governance?”
translations.idiomatic: After showering them with gifts he promoted their sons as well, remarking that turning clients into foster sons did the administration no harm.

sentences.zh: 」先是，司徒韓縯為河內太守，在公無私，所舉一辭而已，後亦不及其門戶，曰：「我舉若可矣，不令恩偏稱一家也。

translations.literal: Before this, Minister of Education Han Yan had been Administrator of Henei; in office he was without private bias—those he recommended he dismissed with a single word, and later did not reach their gates, saying, “If my raising of you suffices, I will not let favor lean to one house alone.”
translations.idiomatic: Minister Han Yan of Henei had taken the opposite tack—purely public recommendations, no follow-up visits—declaring he would not let patronage pool in one clan.

sentences.zh: 」當時論者，或兩譏焉。〉

translations.literal: Discussants of the time sometimes ridiculed both.〉
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries argued both approaches had their faults.〉

sentences.zh: 父異，洛陽令。

translations.literal: His father Yi was magistrate of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu’s father Zhou Yi served as magistrate of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 瑜長壯有姿貌。

translations.literal: Yu was tall and sturdy and had handsome looks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu was a tall, powerfully built man of striking appearance.

sentences.zh: 初，孫堅與義兵討董卓，徙家於舒。

translations.literal: At first, when Sun Jian joined the righteous host to punish Dong Zhuo, he moved his family to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Jian marched west against Dong Zhuo with the coalition army, he resettled his household at Shu.

sentences.zh: 堅子策與瑜同年，獨相友善，瑜推道南大宅以舍策，升堂拜母，有無通共。

translations.literal: Jian’s son Ce was the same year as Yu; alone they were friendly; Yu vacated the great house on the south lane to lodge Ce, ascended the hall to bow to Ce’s mother, and shared whatever they had.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce, born the same year as Zhou Yu, became his closest friend; Zhou gave him the family mansion south of the lane, paid respects to Lady Wu in the hall, and pooled every resource with him.

sentences.zh: 瑜從父尚為丹楊太守，瑜往省之。

translations.literal: Yu’s father’s younger brother Shang was Administrator of Danyang; Yu went to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhou Shang governed Danyang, Zhou Yu went to visit his uncle.

sentences.zh: 會策將東渡，到歷陽，馳書報瑜，瑜將兵迎策。

translations.literal: It happened that Ce was about to cross east; arriving at Liyang he sent a galloping letter to inform Yu; Yu led troops to welcome Ce.
translations.idiomatic: Just as Sun Ce prepared to cross the river east, he wrote from Liyang; Zhou Yu marched out to meet him.

sentences.zh: 策大喜曰：「吾得卿。

translations.literal: Ce was greatly pleased and said, “I have obtained you.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce exclaimed, “Now that I have you—

sentences.zh: 諧也。

translations.literal: It is harmony.”
translations.idiomatic: —the thing is settled.”

sentences.zh: 」遂從攻橫江、當利，皆拔之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he followed in the attack on Hengjiang and Dangli, and both were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Together they stormed Hengjiang and Dangli and carried both forts.

sentences.zh: 乃渡江擊秣陵，破笮融、薛禮。

translations.literal: Then he crossed the river and struck Moling, defeating Ze Rong and Xue Li.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed the Yangzi, stormed Moling, and broke Ze Rong and Xue Li.

sentences.zh: 轉下湖孰、江乘，進入曲阿。

translations.literal: He turned downstream to Hushu and Jiangcheng, advanced into Qu’a.
translations.idiomatic: They swept down through Hushu and Jiangcheng into Qu’a.

sentences.zh: 劉繇奔走，而策之眾已數萬矣。

translations.literal: Liu Yao fled in rout, and Ce’s host already numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao broke and ran while Sun Ce’s army swelled past ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 因謂瑜曰：「吾以此眾取吳會平山越已足。

translations.literal: Thereupon he said to Yu, “With this host I am sufficient to take Wu and Gui and pacify the mountain Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce then told Zhou Yu, “This army is enough to seize Wu and Gui commanderies and subdue the hill tribes.

sentences.zh: 卿還鎮丹楊。

translations.literal: You return to hold Danyang.”
translations.idiomatic: You go back and hold Danyang for me.”

sentences.zh: 」瑜還。

translations.literal: Yu returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu obeyed and withdrew to Danyang.

sentences.zh: 頃之，袁術遣從弟胤代尚為太守，而瑜與尚俱還壽春。

translations.literal: Before long, Yuan Shu sent his cousin Yin to replace Shang as administrator, while Yu and Shang both returned to Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yuan Shu replaced Zhou Shang with his cousin Yuan Yin, so Zhou Yu and his uncle both reported to Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 術欲以瑜為將，瑜觀術終無所成，故求為居巢長，欲假塗東歸，術聽之。

translations.literal: Shu wished to employ Yu as a general; Yu observed that Shu would ultimately accomplish nothing, therefore sought appointment as magistrate of Juchao, intending to borrow the road to return east; Shu permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu wanted Zhou Yu as a general, but Zhou saw no future in him and asked instead for the minor post at Juchao, planning to slip back east through that assignment—and Yuan Shu agreed.

sentences.zh: 遂自居巢還吳。

translations.literal: Thereupon from Juchao he returned to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: From Juchao he made his way home to Wu.

sentences.zh: 是歲，建安三年也。

translations.literal: That year was the third year of Jian’an.
translations.idiomatic: The year was Jian’an 3 (198 CE).

sentences.zh: 策親自迎瑜，授建威中郎將，即與兵二千人，騎五十匹。

translations.literal: Ce personally welcomed Yu and appointed him Colonel of Establishing Might, immediately giving him two thousand troops and fifty horses.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce met him in person, named him colonel of establishing might, and at once handed him two thousand foot and fifty horse.

sentences.zh: 〈《江表傳》曰：策又給瑜鼓吹，為治館舍，贈賜莫與為比。

translations.literal: The Jiang biao zhuan states: Ce also gave Yu military music, built him a residence, and in gifts none could compare.
translations.idiomatic: The *Jiangbiao zhuan* adds that Sun Ce gave him a military band, built him a mansion, and piled on rewards no one else received.

sentences.zh: 策令曰：「周公瑾英俊異才，與孤有總角之好，骨肉之分。

translations.literal: Ce issued an order, saying, “Zhou Gongjin is a hero of outstanding talent; with the orphan he has the friendship of tied hair and the bond of flesh and bone.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce proclaimed that Zhou Yu was a prodigy bound to him since boyhood like bone and blood.

sentences.zh: 如前在丹楊，發眾及船糧以濟大事，論德酬功，此未足以報者也。」〉

translations.literal: As before in Danyang, raising hosts and ships and grain to aid the great enterprise—reckoning virtue and repaying merit—this is not yet enough to repay him.”〉
translations.idiomatic: His earlier levy of men, ships, and grain in Danyang had saved the whole enterprise—no reward could ever balance that debt.”〉

sentences.zh: 瑜時年二十四，吳中皆呼為周郎。

translations.literal: Yu was then twenty-four; all within Wu called him Zhou Lang.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-four he was already “Zhou the Gentleman” to everyone in the southeast.

sentences.zh: 以瑜恩信著於廬江，出備牛渚，後領春谷長。

translations.literal: Because Yu’s kindness and trust were renowned in Lujiang, he went out to garrison Niuzhu, later headed as magistrate of Chungu.
translations.idiomatic: His name for fair dealing won him command at Niuzhu, then the magistracy of Chungu.

sentences.zh: 頃之，策欲取荊州，以瑜為中護軍，領導江夏太守，從攻皖，拔之。

translations.literal: Before long, Ce wished to take Jingzhou; he made Yu Central Protector of the Army, acting as Administrator of Jiangxia, followed in the attack on Wan, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Ce turned toward Jingzhou he named Zhou Yu central protector of the army with acting authority over Jiangxia and brought him on the storming of Wan, which fell.

sentences.zh: 時得橋公兩女，皆國色也。

translations.literal: At that time they obtained the two daughters of Lord Qiao, both of national beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Among the captives were the Qiao sisters, famed as the realm’s great beauties.

sentences.zh: 策自納大橋，瑜納小橋。

translations.literal: Ce himself took the elder Qiao; Yu took the younger Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce married the elder sister; Zhou Yu wed the younger.

sentences.zh: 〈《江表傳》曰：策從容戲瑜曰：「橋公二女雖流離，得吾二人作婿，亦足為歡。」〉

translations.literal: The Jiang biao zhuan states: Ce leisurely teased Yu, saying, “Though Lord Qiao’s two daughters wandered in hardship, to gain us two as sons-in-law is enough for joy.”〉
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce joked that however hard the sisters’ flight, landing two husbands like them was fortune enough.〉

sentences.zh: 復近尋陽，破劉勳，討江夏，還定豫章、廬陵，留鎮巴丘。

translations.literal: Again he drew near Xunyang, defeated Liu Xun, campaigned against Jiangxia, returned to settle Yuzhang and Luling, and remained to garrison Baqiu.
translations.idiomatic: They pushed to Xunyang, crushed Liu Xun, raided Jiangxia, then doubled back to secure Yuzhang and Luling while Zhou Yu held Baqiu.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案：孫策於時始得豫章、廬陵，尚未能得定江夏。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi notes: At that time Ce had only just obtained Yuzhang and Luling and had not yet been able to settle Jiangxia firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi observes that Sun Ce had only just taken Yuzhang and Luling and had not yet fully pacified Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 瑜之所鎮，應在今巴丘縣也，與後所

translations.literal: The place Yu garrisoned ought to be today’s Baqiu county, different from the later
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi argues that the Baqiu where Zhou Yu camped is the county of that name in the west,

translations.literal: (pacified)
translations.idiomatic: not the

sentences.zh: 巴丘處不同。〉

translations.literal: Baqiu site.〉
translations.idiomatic: Baqiu on the lower river associated with later campaigns.〉

sentences.zh: 五年，策薨。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Ce died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Jian’an Sun Ce died.

sentences.zh: 權統事。

translations.literal: Quan took charge of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan assumed leadership of the house.

sentences.zh: 瑜將兵赴喪，遂留吳，以中護軍與長史張昭共掌眾事。

translations.literal: Yu led troops to attend the funeral, then remained in Wu, as Central Protector of the Army together with Chief Clerk Zhang Zhao jointly managing the host of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu marched in for the obsequies and stayed at the capital as central protector of the army, sharing civil and military authority with chief clerk Zhang Zhao.

sentences.zh: 〈《江表傳》曰：曹公新破袁紹，兵威日盛，建安七年，下書責權質任子。

translations.literal: The Jiang biao zhuan states: Lord Cao had newly defeated Yuan Shao and his military awe grew daily; in the seventh year of Jian’an he sent a letter demanding that Quan send a hostage son.
translations.idiomatic: The *Jiangbiao zhuan* relates that after Cao Cao’s victory over Yuan Shao his prestige soared; in Jian’an 7 he demanded a hostage from Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 權召群臣會議，張昭、秦松等猶豫不能決，權意不欲遣質，乃獨將瑜詣母前定議，瑜曰：「昔楚國初封於荊山之側，不滿百里之地，繼嗣賢能，廣土開境，立基於郢，遂據荊楊，至於南海，傳業延祚，九百餘年。

translations.literal: Quan summoned his ministers to deliberate; Zhang Zhao, Qin Song, and others hesitated and could not decide; Quan’s intent was not to send a hostage, so alone he led Yu before his mother to settle the plan. Yu said, “Formerly when Chu was first enfeoffed beside Mount Jing, its land was not a hundred li square; successor after successor was worthy and able, broadened the soil and opened the frontier, founded the base at Ying, then held Jing and Yang as far as the Southern Sea, passed down the enterprise and extended the mandate, more than nine hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan called council; Zhang Zhao and Qin Song wavered while Quan himself refused the demand. Taking Zhou Yu to his mother’s chamber, he heard Zhou argue that tiny Chu had grown across nine centuries by refusing servitude—

sentences.zh: 今將軍承父兄餘資，兼六郡之眾，兵精糧多，將士用命，鑄山為銅，煮海為鹽，境內富饒，人不思亂，汎舟舉帆，朝發夕到，士風勁勇，所向無敵，有何偪迫，而欲送質？

translations.literal: Now the General inherits the surplus resources of father and elder brother, joins the hosts of six commanderies, has crack troops and abundant grain, officers and men obey orders, casts mountains into bronze and boils the sea into salt—within the borders rich and plentiful, men do not think of rebellion; raising sail on a boat, one sets out at dawn and arrives at eve; soldierly vigor is keen and brave, wherever faced none withstand—what compulsion is there that you should wish to send a hostage?
translations.idiomatic: —whereas you command six commanderies, rich arsenals, loyal soldiers, salt and copper wealth, fearless marines—why bend the knee and send a hostage?

sentences.zh: 質一入，不得不與曹氏相首尾，與相首尾，則命召不得不往，便見制於人也。

translations.literal: Once a hostage enters, you cannot but be linked head to tail with the Cao clan; being linked head to tail, when orders summon you cannot but go—you will then be controlled by others.
translations.idiomatic: A hostage would chain you to Cao Cao’s summons forever.

sentences.zh: 極不過一侯印，僕從十餘人，車數乘，馬數匹，豈與南面稱孤同哉？

translations.literal: At the utmost it is no more than a marquis’s seal, a dozen or so attendants, several carriages, several horses—how can it compare with facing south and styling yourself “the orphan”?”
translations.idiomatic: At best you would win a hollow marquis title and a handful of followers—nothing beside ruling your own southland as “this orphan.”

sentences.zh: 不如勿遣，徐觀其變。

translations.literal: Better not to send; slowly observe how matters change.
translations.idiomatic: Better to wait and watch how the north shifts.

sentences.zh: 若曹氏能率義以正天下，將軍事之未晚。

translations.literal: If the Cao clan can lead righteousness to set the realm aright, it will not be late for the General to serve them.
translations.idiomatic: If Cao Cao proves a true restorer of Han, you can still submit later.

sentences.zh: 若圖為暴亂，兵猶火也，不戢將自焚。

translations.literal: If he plots violence and chaos, troops are like fire—if not checked they will burn themselves.
translations.idiomatic: If he turns tyrant, his armies will consume him like unchecked fire.

sentences.zh: 將軍韜勇抗威，以待天命，何送質之有！

translations.literal: The General sheathes courage and opposes might, awaiting Heaven’s mandate—what need is there to send a hostage!”
translations.idiomatic: Stand firm, husband your strength, and await Heaven’s verdict—no hostage is needed!”

sentences.zh: 」權母曰：「公瑾議是也。

translations.literal: Quan’s mother said, “Gongjin’s plan is right.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wu ruled, “Zhou Yu speaks rightly.

sentences.zh: 公瑾與伯符同年，小一月耳，我視之如子也，汝其兄事之。

translations.literal: Gongjin is the same year as Bofu, only a month younger; I look on him as a son—you shall treat him as elder brother.”
translations.idiomatic: He is almost your brother’s age; I count him as a son—serve him as an elder brother.”

sentences.zh: 遂不送質。〉

translations.literal: Thereupon they did not send a hostage.〉
translations.idiomatic: The hostage was never sent.〉

sentences.zh: 十一年，督孫瑜等討麻、保二屯，梟其渠帥，囚俘萬餘口，還備

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he supervised Sun Yu and others in punishing the two stockades Ma and Bao, beheaded their chieftains, took more than ten thousand captives, and returned to garrison
translations.idiomatic: In Jian’an 11 he directed Sun Yu against the Ma and Bao river stockades, beheaded their chiefs, marched home with ten thousand captives, and took position to guard

sentences.zh: （官亭）。

translations.literal: (Guan Pavilion).
translations.idiomatic: the Guan pavilion crossing (the text here is damaged).

sentences.zh: 江夏太守黃祖遣將鄧龍將兵數千人入柴桑，瑜追討擊，生虜龍送吳。

translations.literal: Administrator of Jiangxia Huang Zu sent general Deng Long with several thousand troops into Chaisang; Yu pursued, attacked, captured Deng Long alive, and sent him to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Zu’s general Deng Long raided Chaisang, Zhou Yu ran him down, took him alive, and shipped him to Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 十三年春，權討江夏，瑜為前部大督。

translations.literal: In the spring of the thirteenth year, Quan campaigned against Jiangxia; Yu was Grand Commander of the Van.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Jian’an 13 Sun Quan struck Jiangxia with Zhou Yu as vanguard commander.

sentences.zh: 其年九月，曹公入荊州，劉琮舉眾降，曹公得其水軍，船步兵數十萬，將士聞之皆恐。

translations.literal: That year in the ninth month Lord Cao entered Jingzhou; Liu Cong surrendered the whole host; Cao obtained his navy—several hundred thousand of shipborne and foot soldiers; officers and men heard this and all were afraid.
translations.idiomatic: That September Cao Cao swept into Jingzhou; Liu Cong capitulated with fleet and army—hundreds of thousands of men—and panic spread through Wu.

sentences.zh: 權延見群下，問以計策。

translations.literal: Quan prolonged audience to his host of subordinates and asked for stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan called a full council and demanded plans.

sentences.zh: 議者咸曰：「曹公豺虎也，然託名漢相，挾天子以征四方，動以朝廷為辭，今日拒之，事更不順，且將軍大勢可以拒操者，長江也。

translations.literal: Discussants all said, “Lord Cao is a jackal-tiger; yet he borrows the name of Han chancellor, clasps the Son of Heaven to campaign in the four quarters, and moves always with the court as his pretext—to resist him today would make the affair even less compliant. Moreover the General’s great situation that can resist Cao is the Long River.
translations.idiomatic: Many urged surrender: Cao Cao was a predator hiding behind the Han seal, and Wu’s only shield was the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 今操得荊州，奄有其地。

translations.literal: Now Cao has obtained Jingzhou and suddenly holds its territory.
translations.idiomatic: With Jingzhou in his grasp he now shares the river line.

sentences.zh: 劉表治水軍，蒙沖鬥艦，乃以千數，操悉浮以沿江，兼有步兵，水陸俱下。

translations.literal: Liu Biao built a navy—covered swoopers and fighting ships numbered in the thousands; Cao floats them all along the river, together with foot soldiers, descending by water and land together.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao’s thousands of war junks now row under Cao’s banner beside masses of northern infantry.

sentences.zh: 此為長江之險，已與我共之矣。

translations.literal: This means the Long River’s peril is already shared with us.
translations.idiomatic: The river barrier no longer belongs to us alone.

sentences.zh: 而勢力眾寡，又不可論。

translations.literal: As for strength and numbers, they cannot be compared.
translations.idiomatic: Raw strength is not remotely comparable.

sentences.zh: 愚謂大計不如迎之。

translations.literal: Your servant thinks the great plan is not as good as welcoming him.”
translations.idiomatic: The safest course, they said, was to welcome Cao Cao.”

sentences.zh: 」瑜曰：

translations.literal: Yu said,
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu answered,

sentences.zh: 不然。

translations.literal: It is not so.
translations.idiomatic: “That is wrong.”

sentences.zh: 操雖託名漢相，其實漢賊也。

translations.literal: Though Cao borrows the name of Han chancellor, in truth he is Han’s traitor.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao may call himself chancellor; in truth he is the usurper of Han.

sentences.zh: 將軍以神武雄才，兼仗父兄之烈，割據江東，地方數千里，兵精足用，英雄樂業，尚當橫行天下，為漢家除殘去穢。

translations.literal: The General, with divine martial prowess and heroic talent, moreover relying on the fierce legacy of father and elder brother, has carved out a hold on Jiangdong over several thousand li of territory, has crack troops in sufficient use, heroes gladly serving their office—he ought still to course across the realm and for the House of Han remove cruelty and filth.
translations.idiomatic: You inherit a warrior kingdom thousands of li strong, elite troops, and heroes eager for battle—you should sweep the empire for Han, not grovel to a thief.

sentences.zh: 況操自送死，而可迎之耶？

translations.literal: Moreover when Cao comes to deliver himself to death, how can you welcome him?
translations.idiomatic: He is marching to his own destruction; why receive him as master?

sentences.zh: 請為將軍籌之：今使北土已安，操無內憂，能曠日持久，來爭疆場，又能與我校勝負於船楫，

translations.literal: Allow your servant to reckon for the General: suppose the north were already pacified, Cao had no internal worries, could prolong days and persist in time, come to contest the borderlands, and could also with us compare victory and defeat on oars and rudders—
translations.idiomatic: Picture the worst case: a pacified north, no rebels at Cao Cao’s back, time for a long river campaign, fleets clashing oar to oar—

translations.literal: (Could he)
translations.idiomatic: could he even then

sentences.zh: 乎？

translations.literal: win?”
translations.idiomatic: hope to win?”

sentences.zh: 今北土既未平安，加馬超、韓遂尚在關西，為操後患。

translations.literal: Now the north is not yet peaceful; moreover Ma Chao and Han Sui are still west of the passes, a rear worry for Cao.
translations.idiomatic: But the northwest still boils—Ma Chao and Han Sui threaten his rear.

sentences.zh: 且捨鞍馬，仗舟揖，與吳越爭衡，本非中國所長。

translations.literal: Moreover to abandon saddled horses and rely on oars and poles to contest Wu and Yue is fundamentally not what the Central Plain excels at.
translations.idiomatic: Northern cavalry abandoning the saddle for river war cannot match southern sailors.

sentences.zh: 又今盛寒，馬無蒿草。

translations.literal: Again, now it is bitter cold; horses lack artemisia and grass.
translations.idiomatic: It is deep winter; there is no fodder for the horses on campaign.

sentences.zh: 驅中國士眾遠涉江湖之間不習水土，必生疾病。

translations.literal: Driving hosts of the Central Plain far across rivers and lakes, unaccustomed to water and soil, they are bound to sicken.
translations.idiomatic: Dragging the central armies into malarial rivers will waste them by disease.

sentences.zh: 此數四者，用兵之患也，而操皆冒行之。

translations.literal: These four several items are the worries of employing troops, yet Cao all rashly undertakes them.
translations.idiomatic: These four are classic military blunders—and Cao Cao commits them all.

sentences.zh: 將軍擒操，宜在今日。

translations.literal: For the General to capture Cao ought to be this very day.
translations.idiomatic: Today is the day to break him.

sentences.zh: 瑜請得精兵三萬人，進住夏口，保為將軍破之。

translations.literal: Yu begs to obtain crack troops thirty thousand, advance and encamp at Xiakou, and guarantee for the General to destroy him.
translations.idiomatic: Give me thirty thousand picked men at Xiakou and I will answer for his ruin.”

sentences.zh: 權曰：「老賊欲廢漢自立久矣，陡忌二袁、呂布、劉表與孤耳。

translations.literal: Quan said, “The old traitor has long wished to abolish Han and establish himself; he has only feared the two Yuans, Lü Bu, Liu Biao, and the orphan.”
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan cried, “That old rogue has meant to steal the throne for years—blocked only by the two Yuans, Lü Bu, Liu Biao, and me.”

sentences.zh: 今數雄已滅，惟孤尚存，孤與​​老賊，勢不兩立。

translations.literal: Now those several heroes are destroyed; only the orphan still survives—the orphan and the old traitor cannot both stand.”
translations.idiomatic: Those rivals are gone; only he and I remain—and we cannot share one sky.”

sentences.zh: 君言當擊，甚與孤合，此天以君授孤也。」

translations.literal: Your words that we ought to strike accord greatly with the orphan’s heart; this is Heaven giving you to the orphan.”
translations.idiomatic: Your counsel to fight matches my own heart—Heaven sent you to me.”

sentences.zh: 〈《江表傳》曰：權拔刀斫前奏案曰：「諸將吏敢復有言當迎操者，與此案同！

translations.literal: The Jiang biao zhuan states: Quan drew his sword and chopped the memorial table before him, saying, “Any general or clerk who again speaks of welcoming Cao—shall share this case!”
translations.idiomatic: The *Jiangbiao zhuan* adds that Sun Quan slashed his desk, swearing death to anyone else who mentioned surrender.

sentences.zh: 」及會罷之夜，瑜請見曰：「諸人徒見操書，言水步八十萬，而各恐懾，不復料其虛實，便開此議，甚無謂也。

translations.literal: When the meeting ended that night, Yu requested audience and said, “The host of men only saw Cao’s letter speaking of eight hundred thousand water and foot troops, and each was terrified, no longer weighing its truth or falsehood, then opened this discussion—very meaningless.
translations.idiomatic: That night Zhou Yu asked a private audience: “They panic over Cao’s boast of eight hundred thousand men without counting noses—foolish.”

sentences.zh: 今以實校之，彼所將中國人，不過十五六萬，且軍已久疲，所得表眾，亦極七八萬耳，尚懷狐疑。

translations.literal: Now checking it by the facts, the central-plain troops he brings are no more than a hundred fifty or sixty thousand, and the army has long been weary; the troops he gained from Liu Biao are at most seventy or eighty thousand, and still harbor doubts.
translations.idiomatic: In truth he has perhaps 150,000 northerners, already tired, plus maybe 70,000 Jingzhou conscripts who do not trust him.

sentences.zh: 夫以疲病之卒，御狐疑之眾，眾數雖多，甚未足畏。

translations.literal: With weary, sick soldiers driving doubtful hosts—though the numbers are many, they are hardly to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: Sick veterans herding wavering provincials make a noisy but brittle host.

sentences.zh: 得精兵五萬，自足制之，原將軍勿慮。

translations.literal: Obtain crack troops fifty thousand and they are sufficient to control him; I pray the General not to worry.”
translations.idiomatic: Fifty thousand good men can master him—do not fear.”

sentences.zh: 」權撫背曰：「公瑾，卿言至此，甚合孤心。

translations.literal: Quan stroked his back and said, “Gongjin, that you speak to this point fits the orphan’s heart extremely.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan clasped his shoulder: “Zhou Yu, you read my mind.

sentences.zh: 子布、文表諸人，各顧妻子，挾持私慮，深失所望，獨卿與子敬與孤同耳，此天以卿二人讚孤也。

translations.literal: Zibu, Wenbiao, and the others each look to wife and children, hug private calculations—deeply contrary to what I hoped; only you and Zijing share the orphan’s mind—this is Heaven using you two men to aid the orphan.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao and the rest think only of their households; only you and Lu Su stand with me—Heaven gave me you both.”

sentences.zh: 五萬兵難卒合，已選三萬人，船糧戰具俱辦，卿與子敬、程公便在前發，孤當續發人眾，多載資糧，為卿後援。

translations.literal: Fifty thousand troops are hard to assemble at once; I have already selected thirty thousand—ships, grain, and war gear are all ready—you with Zijing and Lord Cheng shall set out at once in the van; the orphan shall continue to send men and supplies, loading more grain and fodder as your rear support.
translations.idiomatic: He could not raise fifty thousand overnight but had thirty thousand ready with full train—Zhou Yu, Lu Su, and Cheng Pu would sail first while more men and supplies followed.

sentences.zh: 卿能辦之者誠決，邂逅不如意，便還就孤，孤當與孟德決之。

translations.literal: If you can settle it, decide it resolutely; if by chance matters go wrong, return to the orphan—the orphan will join battle with Mengde.”
translations.idiomatic: Win if you can; if fortune turns, fall back on me—I will face Cao Cao myself.”

sentences.zh: 」臣松之以為建計拒曹公，實始魯肅。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi considers that the plan to resist Lord Cao in truth began with Lu Su.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes that the first voice for defying Cao Cao was actually Lu Su’s.

sentences.zh: 於時周瑜使鄱陽，肅勸權呼瑜，瑜使鄱陽還，但與肅闇同，故能共成大勳。

translations.literal: At that time Zhou Yu had been sent to Poyang; Su urged Quan to summon Yu; Yu returned from Poyang, only in secret accord with Su, and therefore they could together accomplish the great merit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu had been posted to Poyang; Lu Su had him recalled so that, once Zhou returned, he and Lu could align in secret and win the great victory together.

sentences.zh: 本傳直云，權延見群下，問以計策，瑜擺撥眾人之議，獨言抗拒之計，了不云肅先有謀，殆為攘肅之善也。〉

translations.literal: The main biography states only that Quan prolonged audience to his subordinates and asked stratagems, that Yu brushed aside the multitude’s discussion and alone spoke the plan of resistance—it does not at all say that Su had the plan first; probably this is to strip away Su’s credit.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes that the main text credits only Zhou Yu’s council-chamber speech and omits Lu Su’s earlier plan—likely a narrative choice that sidelines Lu Su’s priority.

sentences.zh: 時劉備為曹公所破，欲引南渡江。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Bei had been broken by Lord Cao and wished to lead his force south across the river.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei, shattered by Cao Cao, meant to retreat south across the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 與魯肅遇於當陽，遂共圖計，因進住夏口，遣諸葛亮詣權。

translations.literal: He met Lu Su at Dangyang; thereupon they jointly plotted; therefore he advanced and encamped at Xiakou and sent Zhuge Liang to Quan.
translations.idiomatic: At Dangyang he joined Lu Su in strategy, moved up to Xiakou, and sent Zhuge Liang to Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 權遂遣瑜及程普等與備並力逆曹公，遇於赤壁。

translations.literal: Quan thereupon sent Yu and Cheng Pu and others together with Bei to oppose Lord Cao; they met at Chibi.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan dispatched Zhou Yu, Cheng Pu, and allies with Liu Bei to meet Cao Cao at Red Cliffs.

sentences.zh: 時曹公軍眾已有疾病，初一交戰，公軍敗退，引次江北。

translations.literal: At that time Lord Cao’s army masses already had sickness; at the first crossing of arms Lord Cao’s army was defeated and withdrew, leading the line to camp north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Cao’s troops were already sickly; the first clash sent them reeling to the north bank.

sentences.zh: 瑜等在南岸。

translations.literal: Yu and the others were on the south bank.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu held the southern shore.

sentences.zh: 瑜部將黃蓋曰：「今寇眾我寡，難與持久。

translations.literal: Yu’s subordinate general Huang Gai said, “Now the bandits are many and we are few—it is hard to endure long.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Gai warned Zhou Yu: the enemy outnumbered them and a long stalemate would be ruinous.

sentences.zh: 然觀操軍船艦，首尾相接，可燒而走也。

translations.literal: Yet observing Lord Cao’s army ships, stem linked to stern, we can burn them and rout them.”
translations.idiomatic: Yet Cao’s fleet was chained stem to stern—fire ships could scatter it.”

sentences.zh: 」乃取蒙沖鬥艦數十艘，實以薪草，膏油灌其中。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took several tens of covered swoopers and fighting ships, filled them with firewood and grass, and poured fat oil into them.
translations.idiomatic: They loaded dozens of war junks with kindling, straw, and lamp oil.

sentences.zh: 裹以帷幕，上建牙旗，先書報曹公，欺以欲降。

translations.literal: Wrapped them in curtains, raised signal banners on top, first wrote reporting to Lord Cao, deceiving him with intent to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: They draped the hulls, flew command flags, and sent a letter feigning defection.

sentences.zh: 〈《江表傳》載蓋書曰：「蓋受孫氏厚恩，常為將帥，見遇不薄。

translations.literal: The Jiang biao zhuan records Gai’s letter: “Gai has received deep favor from the Sun house, always served as commander, and been treated not thinly.
translations.idiomatic: The *Jiangbiao zhuan* preserves Huang Gai’s forged letter of surrender to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 然顧天下事有大勢，用江東六郡山越之人，以當中國百萬之眾，眾寡不敵，海內所共見也。

translations.literal: Yet looking at the great trend of affairs under heaven, to use the men of six Wu commanderies and the mountain Yue against the central plain’s million hosts—few cannot match many is what all within the seas together sees.
translations.idiomatic: It pleaded that six southern commanderies could not forever hold off a million northern soldiers.

sentences.zh: 東方將吏，無有愚智，皆知其不可，惟周瑜、魯肅偏懷淺戇，意未解耳。

translations.literal: Eastern officers and clerks, none foolish or wise, all know it cannot be done—only Zhou Yu and Lu Su harbor shallow obstinacy and have not understood.”
translations.idiomatic: Every Wu officer knew the odds—only Zhou Yu and Lu Su were painted as stubborn fools.”

sentences.zh: 今日歸命，是其實計。

translations.literal: Today’s submission to the mandate is the true plan.
translations.idiomatic: Surrender, the letter claimed, was the sober choice.

sentences.zh: 瑜所督領，自易摧破。

translations.literal: What Yu commands and leads is itself easy to smash and break.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu’s line, it said, could be broken at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 交鋒之日，蓋為前部，當因事變化，效命在近。

translations.literal: On the day blades cross, Gai shall be the van and shall according to circumstance change and offer his life close at hand.”
translations.idiomatic: Huang Gai promised to turn the battle the moment the fleets met.”

sentences.zh: 」曹公特見行人，密問之，口敕曰：「但恐汝詐耳。

translations.literal: Lord Cao specially saw the messenger and questioned him in secret, orally instructing, “I only fear you are deceiving.”
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao interviewed the envoy in secret, muttering that he feared a ruse.

sentences.zh: 蓋若信實，當授爵賞，超於前後也。」〉

translations.literal: If Gai is trustworthy in truth, I shall confer rank and reward surpassing those before and after.”〉
translations.idiomatic: If Huang Gai meant it, Cao promised rewards above any other defector.”〉

sentences.zh: 又豫備走舸，各系大船後，因引次俱前。

translations.literal: Again he prepared fleeing light boats, each tied behind a great ship; therefore he led the line and all advanced together.
translations.idiomatic: Fast skiffs trailed the fire ships, ready to row the crews clear once the blaze caught.

sentences.zh: 曹公軍吏士皆延頸觀望，指言蓋降。

translations.literal: Lord Cao’s army clerks and soldiers all stretched their necks watching, pointing and saying Gai was surrendering.
translations.idiomatic: Cao’s men lined the rail, craning to watch “Huang Gai come over.”

sentences.zh: 蓋放諸船，同時發火。

translations.literal: Gai released the ships and at the same time set fire.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Gai cut the cables and the whole line burst into flame.

sentences.zh: 時風盛猛，悉延燒岸上營落。

translations.literal: At that time the wind was fierce and strong; all spread burning to the shore camps.
translations.idiomatic: A gale whipped the fire into the northern shore camps.

sentences.zh: 頃之。

translations.literal: Before long.
translations.idiomatic: Moments later,

sentences.zh: 煙炎張天，人馬燒溺死者甚眾，軍遂敗退，還保南郡。

translations.literal: Smoke and flame filled the sky; men and horses burned and drowned—dead extremely many; the army thereupon was defeated and withdrew, returning to defend Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Smoke blotted out the sky; men and horses burned or drowned by thousands; Cao’s host fled toward Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 〈《江表傳》曰：至戰日，蓋先取輕利艦十舫，載燥荻枯柴積其中，灌以魚膏，赤幔覆之，建旌旗龍幡於艦上。

translations.literal: The Jiang biao zhuan states: On the day of battle Gai first took ten light swift ships, loaded dry reeds and kindling heaped within, poured fish oil, covered them with crimson curtains, and raised signal banners and dragon streamers on the ships.
translations.idiomatic: The *Jiangbiao zhuan* adds detail: ten fast boats stacked with oiled reeds under red awnings, dragon pennants snapping.

sentences.zh: 時東南風急，因以十艦最著前，中江舉帆，蓋舉火白諸校，使眾兵齊聲大叫曰：「降焉！

translations.literal: At that time the southeast wind was urgent; therefore the ten ships were placed foremost; midriver they raised sail; Gai raised fire to signal the colonels and made the massed troops together shout loudly, saying, “We surrender!”
translations.idiomatic: A southeast wind drove the decoy squadron midstream; Huang Gai’s torch was the signal for a thunderous cry of “Surrender!”

sentences.zh: 」操軍人皆出營立觀。

translations.literal: Lord Cao’s soldiers all came out of camp and stood watching.
translations.idiomatic: Cao’s men poured from their tents to watch the show.

sentences.zh: 去北軍二里餘，同時發火，火烈風猛，往船如箭，飛埃絕爛，燒盡北船，延及岸邊營柴。

translations.literal: More than two li from the northern army they at the same time set fire; the fire was fierce and the wind strong; the advancing ships were like arrows; flying ash and utter blaze burned up the northern ships and reached the shore-side camp kindling.
translations.idiomatic: Two li from Cao’s lines the torches went up; wind and flame turned the chained fleet into an arrow of fire that consumed shore batteries as well.

sentences.zh: 瑜等率輕銳尋繼其後，雷鼓大進，北軍大壞，曹公退走。〉

translations.literal: Yu and others led light crack troops seeking to follow after them, thundered drums and advanced greatly; the northern army was greatly broken; Lord Cao withdrew and fled.〉
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu’s light infantry swept in behind the drums; the northern army collapsed and Cao Cao ran.〉

sentences.zh: 備與瑜等復共追。

translations.literal: Bei together with Yu and others again jointly pursued.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei joined Zhou Yu in the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 曹公留曹仁等守江陵城。

translations.literal: Lord Cao left Cao Ren and others to guard Jiangling city.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao left Cao Ren to hold Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 逕自北歸。

translations.literal: He himself returned north.
translations.idiomatic: He himself rode north.

sentences.zh: 瑜與程普又進南郡，與仁相對，各隔大江。

translations.literal: Yu together with Cheng Pu again advanced on Nan commandery, facing Ren, each separated by the great river.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu and Cheng Pu pressed Nan commandery, facing Cao Ren across the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 兵未交鋒，

translations.literal: Troops had not yet crossed blades,
translations.idiomatic: Before the armies had crossed steel,

sentences.zh: 〈《吳錄》曰：備謂瑜云：「仁守江陵城，城中糧多，足為疾害。

translations.literal: The Wu lu states: Bei said to Yu, “Ren guards Jiangling city; grain inside the city is abundant—enough to be a swift harm.
translations.idiomatic: The *Wu lu* quotes Liu Bei telling Zhou Yu that Cao Ren’s well-stocked Jiangling was a standing threat.

sentences.zh: 使張益德將千人隨卿，卿分二千人追我，相為從夏水人截仁後，仁聞吾入必走。

translations.literal: Let Zhang Yide lead a thousand men with you; you divide two thousand men to pursue me—we shall mutually from the Xia waters enter and cut Ren’s rear; when Ren hears I have entered he is sure to flee.”
translations.idiomatic: He proposed Zhang Fei reinforce Zhou Yu while Liu Bei looped up the Xia River to strike Cao Ren’s rear.

sentences.zh: 」瑜以二千人益之。〉

translations.literal: Yu with two thousand men augmented him.〉
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu added two thousand men to his column.〉

sentences.zh: 瑜即遣甘寧前據夷陵。

translations.literal: Yu immediately sent Gan Ning forward to occupy Yiling.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu ordered Gan Ning to seize Yiling first.

sentences.zh: 仁分兵騎別攻圍寧。

translations.literal: Ren divided troops and cavalry separately to attack and besiege Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Ren detached horse and foot to surround Gan Ning.

sentences.zh: 寧告急於瑜。

translations.literal: Ning urgently reported to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Ning cried for help.

sentences.zh: 瑜用呂蒙計，留淩統以守其後，身與蒙上救寧。

translations.literal: Yu used Lü Meng’s plan, left Ling Tong to guard his rear, personally with Meng went up to rescue Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu adopted Lü Meng’s plan—Ling Tong held the camp while Zhou Yu and Lü Meng lifted the siege.

sentences.zh: 寧圍既解，乃渡屯北岸，剋期大戰。

translations.literal: When Ning’s siege was already lifted, he then crossed and encamped on the north bank, setting a date for a great battle.
translations.idiomatic: Once Gan Ning was free, Zhou Yu crossed to the north bank and fixed a day for the decisive clash.

sentences.zh: 瑜親跨馬擽陳，會流矢中右脅，瘡甚，便還。

translations.literal: Yu personally mounted a horse and pressed the battle line; it happened that a stray arrow struck his right ribs; the wound was severe and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu rode the line until a stray bolt pierced his right side; the wound drove him from the field.

sentences.zh: 後仁聞瑜臥未起，勒兵就陳。

translations.literal: Later when Ren heard that Yu lay ill and had not risen, he led troops toward the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Zhou Yu was bedridden, Cao Ren marched out to provoke battle.

sentences.zh: 瑜乃自興，案行軍營，激揚吏士，仁由是遂退。

translations.literal: Yu thereupon rose himself, inspected and walked the army camps, roused clerks and soldiers, and Ren thereupon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu had himself carried on rounds of the camps, rallied the ranks, and Cao Ren withdrew.

sentences.zh: 權拜瑜偏將軍，領南郡太守。

translations.literal: Quan appointed Yu Lieutenant General, leading Administrator of Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan named him lieutenant general and governor of Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 以下雋、漢昌、劉陽、州陵為奉邑，屯據江陵。

translations.literal: With Xiajun, Hanchang, Liuyang, and Zhouling as fief income, he encamped and held Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He drew revenue from Xiajun, Hanchang, Liuyang, and Zhouling while headquarters stayed at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 劉備以左將軍領荊州牧，治公安，備詣京見權，瑜上疏曰：「劉備以梟雄之姿，而有關羽、張飛熊虎之將，必非久屈為人用者。

translations.literal: Liu Bei as General of the Left led Jingzhou Shepherd, administering Gong’an; Bei went to the capital to see Quan; Yu submitted a memorial saying, “Liu Bei with the bearing of a fierce raptor, moreover having Guan Yu and Zhang Fei as bear-and-tiger generals, is surely not one who will long bend to serve under others.”
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei visited Sun Quan as shepherd of Jingzhou from Gong’an, Zhou Yu warned that Liu’s genius and his tiger generals Guan Yu and Zhang Fei would not long serve a master.

sentences.zh: 愚謂大計宜徙備置吳，盛為築宮室，多其美女玩好，以娛其耳目，分此二人，各置一方，使如瑜者得挾與攻戰，大事可定也。

translations.literal: Your servant’s foolish opinion on the great plan is that it is fitting to move Bei and settle him in Wu, greatly build palaces and chambers for him, increase beauties and playthings to delight his ears and eyes, divide these two men and place each in a separate quarter, so that one like your servant could assist in attacking—then the great affair can be settled.”
translations.idiomatic: He urged Sun Quan to house Liu Bei in the capital, distract him with luxury, and split him from his generals so Wu could control him.

sentences.zh: 今猥割土地以資業之，聚此三人，俱在疆場，恐蛟龍得雲雨，終非池中物也。

translations.literal: Now rashly cutting off land to enrich their enterprise, gathering these three men all on the border field—I fear when the horned dragon obtains cloud and rain it will in the end not be a creature of the pond.”
translations.idiomatic: Ceding territory instead would arm all three on the frontier—dragons that would leave the pool once storm clouds gather.”

sentences.zh: 」權以曹公在北方，當廣攬英雄，又恐備難卒制，故不納。

translations.literal: Quan because Lord Cao was in the north and ought broadly to gather heroes, and again feared Bei would be hard to control at once, therefore did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan, needing allies against Cao Cao and doubting he could cage Liu Bei, rejected the scheme.

sentences.zh: 是時劉璋為益州牧。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Zhang was Shepherd of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Liu Zhang held Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 外有張魯寇侵，瑜乃詣京見權曰：「今曹操新折衄，方憂在腹心，未能與將軍連兵相事也。

translations.literal: Outside there was Zhang Lu’s raiding invasion; Yu therefore went to the capital to see Quan and said, “Now Cao Cao is newly broken and bruised; his cares lie in his belly and heart—he is not able to join arms with the General in mutual service.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu told Sun Quan that Cao Cao, smarting from defeat, could not mount a joint campaign—

sentences.zh: 乞與奮威俱進取蜀，得蜀而並張魯，因留奮威固守其地，好與馬超結援。

translations.literal: I beg together with General Who Displays Might to advance and take Shu; obtaining Shu and annexing Zhang Lu, then leave General Who Displays Might firmly to guard that ground and happily ally with Ma Chao as aid.
translations.idiomatic: —and begged to march west with Sun Yu, general who displays might, seize Shu and Zhang Lu, leave Sun Yu to hold the west, and link Ma Chao against the north.

sentences.zh: 瑜還與將軍據襄陽以蹙操，北方可圖也。

translations.literal: Yu returning with the General would hold Xiangyang to press Lord Cao—the north could then be planned.”
translations.idiomatic: He would then return with Sun Quan to squeeze Xiangyang and open a path against the central plain.”

sentences.zh: 」權許之。

translations.literal: Quan granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan approved the western expedition.

sentences.zh: 瑜還江陵為行裝，而道於巴丘病卒，

translations.literal: Yu returned to Jiangling to prepare traveling gear, but on the road at Baqiu died of illness,
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu went back to Jiangling to fit out the army and died of illness at Baqiu on the way.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案，瑜欲取蜀，還江陵治嚴，所卒之處，應在今之巴陵，與前所鎮巴丘，名同處異也。〉

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi notes: When Yu wished to take Shu, returned to Jiangling to ready strict order, the place where he died ought to be today’s Baling—same name Baqiu as before but a different place.〉
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi argues the Baqiu where Zhou Yu died is modern Baling, not the earlier Baqiu garrison.〉

sentences.zh: 時年三十六。

translations.literal: His years were thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He was thirty-six years old.

sentences.zh: 權素服舉哀。

translations.literal: Quan in plain garb raised mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan donned mourning and wept for him.

sentences.zh: 感動左右。

translations.literal: It moved those to his left and right.
translations.idiomatic: His grief moved everyone at court.

sentences.zh: 喪當還吳，又迎之蕪湖，眾事費度，一為供給。

translations.literal: When the funeral was to return to Wu, he again welcomed it at Wuhu; for all affairs of expense and planning, in one stroke he supplied.
translations.idiomatic: He met the catafalque at Wuhu and paid every cost of the obsequies.

sentences.zh: 後著令曰：「故將軍周瑜、程普，其有人客，皆不得問。」

translations.literal: Later he issued an order saying, “For the former generals Zhou Yu and Cheng Pu, if they have retainers and guests, none shall be questioned.”
translations.idiomatic: He later decreed that Zhou Yu’s and Cheng Pu’s old retainers would not be audited for tax or service.

sentences.zh: 初瑜見友於策，太妃又使權以兄奉之。

translations.literal: At first Yu was befriended by Ce; the Senior Lady again ordered Quan to serve him as elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce had befriended him, and Lady Wu told Sun Quan to honor him as an elder brother.

sentences.zh: 是時權位為將軍，諸將賓客為禮尚簡，而瑜獨先盡敬，便執臣節。

translations.literal: At that time Quan’s position was general; for the generals and retainers the rites were still simple, yet Yu alone first showed full respect and then held minister ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan was still only a general, other officers kept casual manners; Zhou Yu alone offered him full ministerial deference.

sentences.zh: 性度恢廓，大率為得人，惟與程普不睦。

translations.literal: His nature and measure were vast and broad; for the most part he won men—only with Cheng Pu was he not harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: He was magnanimous and usually won loyalty, though he clashed with Cheng Pu.

sentences.zh: 〈《江表傳》曰：普頗以年長，數陵侮瑜。

translations.literal: The Jiang biao zhuan states: Pu, relying somewhat on senior years, repeatedly insulted and bullied Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The *Jiangbiao zhuan* says Cheng Pu, as senior officer, habitually slighted Zhou Yu.

sentences.zh: 瑜折節容下，終不與校。

translations.literal: Yu bent his measure to tolerate subordinates and in the end did not contest with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu swallowed pride and never answered in kind.

sentences.zh: 普後自敬服而親重之，乃告人曰：「與周公瑾交，若飲醇醪，不覺自醉。

translations.literal: Later Pu of himself came to respect and serve him and treated him with intimacy and weight, then told people, “To associate with Zhou Gongjin is like drinking fine mash—without realizing it you grow drunk.”
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Pu later admitted that friendship with Zhou Yu was like sipping aged wine—you warmed to it before you knew.

sentences.zh: 」時人以其謙讓服人如此。

translations.literal: People of the time because of this submitted to him in modesty thus.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries honored him for that humility.

sentences.zh: 初曹公聞瑜年少有美才，謂可遊說動也，乃密下揚州，遣九江蔣幹往見瑜。

translations.literal: At first when Lord Cao heard that Yu was young and had fine talent, he judged that he could be moved by persuasion; therefore he secretly issued orders to Yangzhou and sent Jiang Gan of Jiujiang to go see Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao, hearing Zhou Yu was young, sent Jiang Gan of Jiujiang south to talk him over.

sentences.zh: 幹有儀容，以才辯見稱，獨步江、淮之間，莫與為對。

translations.literal: Gan had bearing in appearance and by eloquent disputation was praised; alone he walked between the Yangzi and Huai—none could match him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Gan was famous between the Yangzi and Huai for looks and tongue.

sentences.zh: 乃布衣葛巾，自託私行詣瑜。

translations.literal: Thereupon in plain cloth and ge cloth headwrap he entrusted himself to a private journey to visit Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed in scholar’s dress, pretending a private call.

sentences.zh: 瑜出迎之，立謂幹曰：「子翼良苦，遠涉江湖為曹氏作說客邪？

translations.literal: Yu came out to welcome him, stood and said to Gan, “Ziyi has toiled bitterly—have you crossed rivers and lakes to play lobbyist for the Cao clan?”
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu met him with, “Ziyi, you have come a long way to plead Cao Cao’s case.”

sentences.zh: 」幹曰：「吾與足下州里，中間別隔，遙聞芳烈，故來敘闊，並觀雅規，而云說客，無乃逆詐乎？

translations.literal: Gan said, “I and you, sir, are from the same province; in the middle we were separated; from afar I heard your fragrant deeds, therefore I have come to renew old ties and also to observe your elegant rule—and you call me lobbyist; is that not reverse suspicion?”
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Gan protested that he came only as a fellow townsman to pay respects.

sentences.zh: 」瑜曰：「吾雖不及夔、曠，聞弦賞音，足知雅曲也。

translations.literal: Yu said, “Though I do not reach Kui and Kuang, hearing the strings I appreciate the tone—enough to know the elegant tune.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu answered that he could still hear a false note in any tune.

sentences.zh: 」因延幹入，為設酒食。

translations.literal: Thereupon he extended Gan entry and for him set out wine and food.
translations.idiomatic: He led him in and feasted him.

sentences.zh: 畢，遣之曰：「適吾有密事，且出就館，事了，別自相請。

translations.literal: When finished he sent him away, saying, “Just now I have secret business; for the moment go out to the lodge; when the affair is finished I shall separately invite you myself.”
translations.idiomatic: After dinner he excused himself and told Jiang Gan to wait at the guest lodge.

sentences.zh: 」後三日，瑜請幹與周觀營中，行視倉庫軍資器仗訖，還宴飲，示之侍者服飾珍玩之物，因謂幹曰：「丈夫處世，遇知己之主，外託君臣之義，內結骨肉之恩，言行計從，禍福共之，假使蘇張更生，酈叟復出，猶撫其背而折其辭，豈足下幼生所能移乎？

translations.literal: After three days Yu invited Gan together with him to tour the camps; he walked and inspected storehouses, army supplies, and weapons to completion, returned and feasted and drank, showed him the attire, ornaments, and rare playthings of his attendants, and thereupon said to Gan, “A great man in the world, meeting a lord who knows him, outwardly entrusts the righteousness of lord and minister, inwardly ties the kindness of flesh and bone—words go and plans follow, misfortune and fortune are shared; even if Su and Qin were reborn or the old man of Li appeared again, still I would stroke their backs and break their rhetoric—how could the likes of you, born yesterday, move me?”
translations.idiomatic: Three days later he marched Jiang Gan through arsenals and treasure, then said no Su Qin could sway a man who had found such a lord.

sentences.zh: 」幹但笑，終無所言。

translations.literal: Gan only laughed and in the end spoke nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Gan smiled and said nothing more.

sentences.zh: 幹還，稱瑜雅量高致，非言辭所間。

translations.literal: When Gan returned, he praised Yu’s high capacity and far aim—not to be sundered by words.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the north Jiang Gan reported that Zhou Yu’s integrity could not be bought with words.

sentences.zh: 中州之士，亦以此多之。

translations.literal: Gentlemen of the central plain for this reason also thought much of him.
translations.idiomatic: Northerners respected him the more for it.

sentences.zh: 劉備之自京還也，權乘飛雲大船，與張昭、秦松、魯肅等十餘人共追送之，大宴會敘別。

translations.literal: When Liu Bei was returning from the capital, Quan rode a great ship Flying Cloud and together with Zhang Zhao, Qin Song, Lu Su, and more than ten others jointly pursued to see him off, holding a great banquet to speak of parting.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei left the capital, Sun Quan chased his boat in the Flying Cloud with a dozen ministers and threw him a farewell feast.

sentences.zh: 昭、肅等先出，權獨與備留語，因言次，嘆瑜曰：「公瑾文武籌略，萬人之英，顧其器量廣大，恐不久為人臣耳。

translations.literal: Zhao, Su, and others first went out; Quan alone remained speaking with Bei; taking advantage of the turn in talk he sighed concerning Yu, saying, “Gongjin’s civil and military planning and strategy make him the hero of ten thousand men—yet looking at his vast capacity, I fear he will not long remain another’s subject.”
translations.idiomatic: Alone with Liu Bei afterward, Sun Quan sighed that Zhou Yu’s genius was so vast he might not stay a vassal forever.

sentences.zh: 」瑜之破魏軍也，曹公曰：「孤不羞走。

translations.literal: When Yu broke the Wei army, Lord Cao said, “The orphan is not ashamed to flee.”
translations.idiomatic: After Red Cliffs Cao Cao admitted he was not ashamed to have run.

sentences.zh: 」後書與權曰：「赤壁之役，值有疾病，孤燒船自退，橫使周瑜虛獲此名。

translations.literal: Later he wrote Quan saying, “In the Chibi campaign, it happened that I had sickness; the orphan burned ships and withdrew of himself—horizontally letting Zhou Yu vainly obtain this name.”
translations.idiomatic: He later wrote Sun Quan claiming he had burned his own ships and withdrawn—letting Zhou Yu steal empty glory.

sentences.zh: 」瑜威聲遠著，故曹公、劉備咸欲疑譖之。

translations.literal: Yu’s awe-inspiring name was far established; therefore Lord Cao and Liu Bei both wished to doubt and slander him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu’s fame was so great that both Cao Cao and Liu Bei tried to sow doubt about him.

sentences.zh: 及卒，權流涕曰：「公瑾有王佐之資，今忽短命，孤何賴哉！

translations.literal: When he died, Quan wept and said, “Gongjin had the stuff of a king’s assistant; now suddenly short life—what does the orphan rely on!”
translations.idiomatic: At his death Sun Quan wept that Heaven had robbed him of a pillar fit for an emperor.

sentences.zh: 」後權稱尊號，謂公卿曰：「孤非周公瑾，不帝矣。」〉

translations.literal: Later when Quan assumed the imperial title he said to the Excellencies and ministers, “Without Zhou Gongjin the orphan would not have become emperor.”〉
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan took the throne he told his court he would never have been emperor without Zhou Yu.〉

sentences.zh: 瑜少精意於音樂。

translations.literal: In his youth Yu concentrated intent on music.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Zhou Yu trained a musician’s ear.

sentences.zh: 雖三爵之後，其有闕誤。

translations.literal: Even after three goblets of wine, if there was a slip or error,
translations.idiomatic: Even deep in his cups, if a note slipped,

sentences.zh: 瑜必知之，知之必顧，故時人謠曰：「曲有誤，周郎顧。」

translations.literal: Yu was sure to know it; knowing it he was sure to glance—therefore people of the time rhymed, “When the tune slips, Zhou Lang glances.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu’s head would turn—hence the rhyme: “Miss the tune—Zhou Lang’s eyes.”

sentences.zh: 瑜兩男一女，女配太子登。

translations.literal: Yu had two sons and one daughter; the daughter was matched to Heir Deng.
translations.idiomatic: He left two sons and a daughter; the girl married crown prince Sun Deng.

sentences.zh: 男循尚公主，拜騎都尉，有瑜風，早卒。

translations.literal: The son Xun married the princess and was appointed Commandant of Cavalry; he had Yu’s manner and died early.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xun wed a princess, became cavalry commandant, showed his father’s dash, and died young.

sentences.zh: 循弟胤，初拜興業都尉。

translations.literal: Xun’s younger brother Yin at first was appointed Commandant of Prospering Enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Zhou Yin first held the post of commandant of prospering enterprise.

sentences.zh: 妻以宗女，授兵千人，屯公安。

translations.literal: He was given a daughter of the imperial clan as wife, was granted a thousand troops, and encamped at Gong’an.
translations.idiomatic: He married an imperial clanswoman, commanded a thousand men at Gong’an.

sentences.zh: 黃龍元年，封都鄉侯，後以罪徙廬陵郡。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huanglong he was enfeoffed Marquis of Duxiang village; later because of crime he was moved to Luling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Huanglong 1 made him village marquis of Duxiang; later a crime sent him into exile in Luling.

sentences.zh: 赤烏二年，諸葛瑾、步騭連名上疏曰：

translations.literal: In the second year of Chiwu Zhuge Jin and Bu Zhi jointly submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In Chiwu 2 Zhuge Jin and Bu Zhi filed a joint memorial:

sentences.zh: 故將軍周瑜子胤，昔蒙粉飾，受封為將，不能養之以福，思立功效，至縱情慾，招速罪辟。

translations.literal: The former general Zhou Yu’s son Yin, in former times receiving adornment, received enfeoffment as a general; unable to nurture him with blessing, he thought to set up merit and effect, until he indulged passion and desire and hastened punishment and law.
translations.idiomatic: They pleaded for Zhou Yin, once honored as a general, who had fallen into debauchery and exile.

sentences.zh: 臣竊以瑜昔見寵任，入作心膂，出為爪牙，銜命出征，身當矢石，盡節用命，視死如歸。

translations.literal: Your servant privately considers that Yu in former times received favor and trust—within he served as heart and liver, without he served as talons and fangs; biting mandate he went on campaign, personally faced flying stones, exhausted loyalty and obeyed orders, looked on death as return home.
translations.idiomatic: They reminded the throne that Zhou Yu had been Sun Quan’s right hand—bearing arrows in battle and treating death as home.

sentences.zh: 故能摧曹操於烏林，走曹仁於郢都，揚國威德，華夏是震，蠢爾蠻荊，莫不賓服。

translations.literal: Therefore he was able to crush Cao Cao at Wulin, drive Cao Ren from Yingdu, raise the state's awe and virtue so that the Hua-Xia trembled; stupid though barbarian Jing might be, none failed to submit.
translations.idiomatic: He broke Cao Cao at Wulin, drove Cao Ren from Jiangling, shook the north, and brought every southern chief to heel.

sentences.zh: 雖周之方叔，漢之信、布，誠無以尚也。

translations.literal: Though Zhou's Fangshu or Han's Xin and Bu—truly none could surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: Not even Zhou's Fangshu or Han's Han Xin and Ying Bu could top him.

sentences.zh: 夫折沖扦難之臣，自古帝王莫不貴重，故漢高帝封爵之誓曰『使黃河如帶，太山如礪，國以永存，爰及苗裔』。

translations.literal: As for ministers who blunt the foe and ward off peril, from antiquity emperors and kings have all prized them; therefore Han Gaozu in his oath enfeoffing nobles said, 'Let the Yellow River be like a belt, Mount Tai like a whetstone—the state shall endure forever, reaching to descendants.'
translations.idiomatic: Frontier-breaking ministers have always been treasured—Gaozu swore that noble houses would last as long as river and mountain.

sentences.zh: 申以丹書，重以盟詛，藏於宗廟，傳於無窮，欲使功臣之後，世世相踵，非徒子孫，乃關苗裔，報德明功，勤勤懇懇，如此之至，欲以勸戒後人，用命之臣，死而無悔也。

translations.literal: He repeated it with vermilion writing, weighted it with blood-oath curse, stored it in the ancestral temple, passed it endless—wishing that merit ministers' posterity generation after generation should follow in succession, not only sons and grandsons but even collateral lines, repaying virtue and clarifying merit, diligent and earnest to this extreme—wishing thereby to warn and instruct later men so that ministers who obeyed orders might die without regret.
translations.idiomatic: Those oaths, written in red and sealed in blood, hung in the temple so every generation would remember the debt to loyal servants.

sentences.zh: 況於瑜身沒未久，而其子胤降為匹夫，益可悼傷。

translations.literal: Moreover when Yu's body had not long been gone and his son Yin was reduced to commoner status, it is all the more pitiable.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhou Yu is barely cold in the grave while his son Yin has been cast down to a private—doubly cruel.

sentences.zh: 竊惟陛下欽明稽古，隆於興繼，為胤歸訴，乞丐餘罪，還兵復爵，使失旦之雞，復得鳴。

translations.literal: Your servant privately considers that Your Majesty is reverent and bright, investigates antiquity, and elevates revival; for Yin he returns plea, begs pardon for remaining crime, restores troops and rank, so that the cock that missed dawn may crow again.
translations.idiomatic: They begged the wise sovereign to revive the Zhou house's honor—restore Yin's command and title so the silenced rooster may crow again.

sentences.zh: 抱罪之臣，展其後效。

translations.literal: Let the minister who bears guilt unfold later merit.
translations.idiomatic: Let a penitent servant prove himself anew.

sentences.zh: 權答曰：「腹心舊勳，與孤協事，公瑾有之，誠所不忘。

translations.literal: Quan answered, saying, 'Heart-and-belly old merit who with the orphan cooperated in affairs—Gongjin had it; truly I do not forget.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan answered that Zhou Yu had been his true confederate—never forgotten.

sentences.zh: 昔胤年少，初無功勞，橫受精兵，爵以侯將，蓋念公瑾以及於胤也。

translations.literal: Formerly Yin was young, at first without merit or toil, yet horizontally received crack troops, rank as marquis general—it was thinking of Gongjin and extending it to Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yin had been young and untried when Sun Quan gave him troops and a marquis's rank purely for his father's sake.

sentences.zh: 而胤恃此，酗淫自恣，前後告喻，曾無悛改。

translations.literal: Yet Yin relied on this, drank and debauched at will; before and after admonition, never once reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yin took that favor as license to drink and womanize; warnings never changed him.

sentences.zh: 孤於公瑾，義猶二君，樂胤成就，豈有已哉？

translations.literal: The orphan toward Gongjin, righteousness is still as to two lords; rejoicing in Yin's accomplishment—could there be an end?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan said his bond to Zhou Yu was like kin—he had wanted Zhou Yin to thrive without limit.

sentences.zh: 迫胤罪惡，未宜便還，且欲苦之，使自知耳。

translations.literal: Pressed by Yin's crimes, it was not fitting to return him at once; I wished for the moment to harden him, letting him know himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's crimes made an instant recall wrong; exile was meant to teach him self-knowledge.

sentences.zh: 今二君勤勤援引漢高河山之誓，孤用恧然。

translations.literal: Now you two gentlemen earnestly cite Han Gaozu's oath of river and mountain—the orphan feels ashamed thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Their appeal to Gaozu's river-and-mountain oath shamed him.

sentences.zh: 雖德非其疇，猶欲庶幾，事亦如爾，故未順旨。

translations.literal: Though virtue does not match that class, still I wish to draw near; the affair is likewise, therefore I have not yet followed the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Though his virtue fell short of Gaozu's, he meant to meet them halfway—hence the delay.

sentences.zh: 以公瑾之子，而二君在中間，苟使能改，亦何患乎！

translations.literal: For Gongjin's son, with you two gentlemen in the middle—if he can indeed reform, what worry is there!
translations.idiomatic: He is still Zhou Yu's son, and you stand surety—if he mends his ways, all will be well.

sentences.zh: 」瑾、騭表比上，朱然及全琮亦俱陳乞，權乃許之。

translations.literal: Jin and Zhi repeatedly submitted memorials; Zhu Ran and Quan Zong also jointly pleaded; Quan thereupon granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Jin, Bu Zhi, Zhu Ran, and Quan Zong kept petitioning until Sun Quan relented.

sentences.zh: 會胤病死。

translations.literal: It happened that Yin died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Before Zhou Yin could return, he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 瑜兄子峻，亦以瑜元功為偏將軍，領吏士千人。

translations.literal: Yu's elder brother's son Jun, because of Yu's primal merit, was also Lieutenant General, leading clerks and soldiers a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jun, Zhou Yu's nephew, became lieutenant general for the same founding merit, with a thousand-man command.

sentences.zh: 峻卒，全琮表峻子護為將。

translations.literal: When Jun died, Quan Zong memorialized Jun's son Hu as general.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Jun died, Quan Zong recommended his son Zhou Hu for command.

sentences.zh: 權曰：「昔走曹操，拓有荊州，皆是公瑾，常不忘之。

translations.literal: Quan said, 'Formerly in driving off Cao Cao and expanding to hold Jingzhou—all was Gongjin; I always do not forget it.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan said driving Cao Cao and winning Jingzhou had all been Zhou Yu's work.

sentences.zh: 初聞峻亡，仍欲用護，聞護性行危險，用之適為作禍，故便止之。

translations.literal: At first hearing of Jun's death, I still wished to employ Hu; hearing Hu's nature and conduct were dangerous, employing him would only make disaster—therefore I stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He had meant to favor Zhou Hu until reports of the youth's vicious temper made him withdraw the appointment.

sentences.zh: 孤念公瑾，豈有已乎？」

translations.literal: The orphan's thought of Gongjin—could it have an end?
translations.idiomatic: His debt to Zhou Yu, he said, could never be repaid.

sentences.zh: 魯肅字子敬，臨淮東城人也。

translations.literal: Lu Su, courtesy name Zijing, was a man of Dongcheng in Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su, courtesy Zijing, came from Dongcheng in Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 生而失父，與祖母居。

translations.literal: He was born having lost his father and dwelt with his grandmother.
translations.idiomatic: His father died before he was born; he was raised by his grandmother.

sentences.zh: 家富於財，性好施與，爾時天下已亂，肅不治家事，大散財貨，摽賣田地，以賑窮弊結士為務，甚得鄉邑歡心。

translations.literal: The household was rich in wealth; his nature loved giving and sharing; at that time the realm was already in chaos; Su did not manage household affairs, greatly scattered goods and wealth, put up fields and land for sale, taking relief of the poor and binding knights-errant as his task—he extremely won the joy of township and village.
translations.idiomatic: Rich and generous, he ignored housekeeping while the empire collapsed—sold land, fed the needy, and armed young bravos until his town adored him.

sentences.zh: 周瑜為居巢長，將數百人故過候肅，並求資糧。

translations.literal: Zhou Yu was magistrate of Juchao, leading several hundred men purposely passing to visit Su, and jointly sought provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu, as magistrate of Juchao, detoured hundreds of men to call on Lu Su and beg grain.

sentences.zh: 肅家有兩囷米，各三千斛。

translations.literal: Su's household had two round granaries of rice, each three thousand hu.
translations.idiomatic: The Lu granaries held two thousand-hectolitre bins of rice.

sentences.zh: 肅乃指一囷與周瑜，瑜益知其奇也。

translations.literal: Su thereupon pointed to one bin and gave it to Zhou Yu; Yu all the more knew his extraordinariness.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su pointed at one bin and gave it all to Zhou Yu, who saw his greatness.

sentences.zh: 遂相親結，定僑、札之分。

translations.literal: Thereupon they became intimate and bound, fixing the division of Qiao and Zha.
translations.idiomatic: They swore brotherhood like the ancient paragons Gong Ziqiao and Ji Zha.

sentences.zh: 袁術聞其名，就署東城長。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu heard his name and thereupon appointed him magistrate of Dongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu, hearing his fame, named him magistrate of Dongcheng.

sentences.zh: 肅見術無綱紀，不足與立事，乃攜老弱將輕俠少年百餘人，南到居巢就瑜。

translations.literal: Su saw that Shu lacked regulation and was not worth establishing affairs with; thereupon carrying old and weak he led more than a hundred light-errant youths south to Juchao to join Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su saw Yuan Shu as hopeless, gathered kin and swordsmen, and marched south to Zhou Yu at Juchao.

sentences.zh: 瑜之東渡，因與同行，

translations.literal: When Yu crossed east, therefore he went together with him,
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Yu crossed the river east, Lu Su went with him.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：肅體貌魁奇，少有壯節，好為奇計。

translations.literal: The Book of Wu states: Su's body and appearance were huge and strange; in youth he had stalwart integrity and loved to devise unusual plans.
translations.idiomatic: The *Book of Wu* describes him as huge, odd-looking, bold in youth, and fond of stratagems.

sentences.zh: 天下將亂，乃學擊劍騎射，招聚少年，給其衣食，往來南山中射獵，陰相部勒，講武習兵。

translations.literal: When the realm was about to be in chaos, he then studied sword striking and mounted archery, summoned and gathered youths, supplied their clothes and food, went back and forth in the southern mountains hunting, secretly organized them, lectured on martial arts and drilled troops.
translations.idiomatic: Foreseeing chaos he drilled sword and bow, fed a band of youths, hunted the southern hills with them, and trained them as a private corps.

sentences.zh: 父老咸曰：「魯氏世衰，乃生此狂兒！

translations.literal: The village elders all said, 'The Lu clan's generations decline—yet it produces this mad boy!
translations.idiomatic: Village elders groaned that a declining house had bred a madcap.

sentences.zh: 」後雄傑並起，中州擾亂，肅乃命其屬曰：「中國失綱，寇賊橫暴，淮、泗間非遺種之地，吾聞江東沃野萬里，民富兵強，可以避害，寧肯相隨俱至樂土，以觀時變乎？

translations.literal: 'Later when heroes rose together and the central plain was disturbed, Su then ordered his followers, saying, 'The central state has lost its net; bandits run rampant; between Huai and Si is not a place to leave seed; I have heard the eastern river has fertile wilds ten thousand li, people rich and soldiers strong—we can avoid harm; are you willing to follow together to happy soil and observe how the times change?
translations.idiomatic: When warlords tore the north apart, Lu Su told his people the Huai-Si corridor was death but the lower Yangzi offered refuge—who would follow him south?

sentences.zh: 」其屬皆從命。

translations.literal: His followers all obeyed the order.
translations.idiomatic: Every dependent agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃使細弱在前，強壯在後，男女三百餘人行。

translations.literal: Thereupon he made the delicate weak go in front, the strong stalwart in rear—more than three hundred men and women traveling.
translations.idiomatic: He put women and children in front, fighters in the rear—three hundred souls on the road.

sentences.zh: 州追騎至，肅等徐行，勒兵持滿，謂之曰：「卿等丈夫，當解大數。

translations.literal: When provincial pursuit riders arrived, Su and the others walked slowly, drew bows fully drawn, and said to them, 'You gentlemen are husbands—ought to understand the great reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: When prefectural cavalry caught up, Lu Su's band walked slowly, bows drawn, and shouted that real men should see the big picture.

sentences.zh: 今日天下兵亂，有功弗賞，不追無罰，何為相偪乎？

translations.literal: Today the realm's soldiers are in chaos—those with merit are not rewarded, those not pursued are not punished—why do you press each other?
translations.idiomatic: In this chaos merit goes unrewarded and crime unpunished—why hound harmless refugees?

sentences.zh: 」又自植盾，引弓射之，矢皆洞貫。

translations.literal: Again he himself planted a shield, drew a bow and shot at it—the arrows all pierced through.
translations.idiomatic: He planted a shield and shot it through—every shaft bit clean.

sentences.zh: 騎既嘉肅言，且度不能制，乃相率還。

translations.literal: The riders both admired Su's words and reckoned they could not control him; therefore they mutually led one another back.
translations.idiomatic: The troopers admired his nerve, saw they could not take him, and rode away.

sentences.zh: 肅渡江往見策，策亦雅奇之。〉

translations.literal: Su crossed the river to go see Ce; Ce also thought him extraordinarily strange.〉
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su crossed to meet Sun Ce, who was equally struck by him.〉

sentences.zh: 留家曲阿。

translations.literal: He left his family at Qu'a.
translations.idiomatic: He left his household at Qu'a.

sentences.zh: 會祖母亡，還葬東城。

translations.literal: It happened that his grandmother died; he returned to bury at Dongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When his grandmother died he went home to bury her at Dongcheng.

sentences.zh: 劉子揚與肅友善，遺肅書，曰：「方今天下豪傑並起，吾子姿才，尤宜今日。

translations.literal: Liu Ziyang was friendly with Su and sent Su a letter, saying, 'Now heroes of the realm rise together; you, sir, have talent especially suited to this day.
translations.idiomatic: His friend Liu Ziye wrote urging him to seize the moment.

sentences.zh: 急還迎老母，無事滯於東城。

translations.literal: Hasten back to welcome your old mother; do not idly linger at Dongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Bring your mother south at once—do not molder in Dongcheng.

sentences.zh: 近鄭寶者，今在巢湖，擁眾萬餘，處地肥饒，廬江間人多依就之，況吾徒乎？

translations.literal: Zheng Bao who is near now is at Chao Lake, embracing a host over ten thousand; the ground he occupies is fat and rich; many between Lujiang rely on him—how much more we of your sort?
translations.idiomatic: A warlord named Zheng Bao held ten thousand men on rich ground by Chao Lake—why not join him?

sentences.zh: 觀其形勢，又可博集，時不可失，足下速之。

translations.literal: Observing his situation, one can again gather widely; the time cannot be lost—under your feet, hurry.
translations.idiomatic: The moment was ripe, Liu said—move fast.

sentences.zh: 」肅答然其計。

translations.literal: Su answered, approving his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su wrote back that he would go.

sentences.zh: 葬畢還曲阿，欲北行。

translations.literal: When the burial was finished he returned to Qu'a, intending to go north.
translations.idiomatic: After the funeral he returned to Qu'a, meaning to march north to Zheng Bao.

sentences.zh: 會瑜已徙肅母到吳，肅具以狀語瑜。

translations.literal: It happened that Yu had already moved Su's mother to Wu; Su fully told the circumstances to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu had meanwhile moved Lu Su's mother to Wu; Lu Su told him the whole plan.

sentences.zh: 時孫策已薨，權尚住吳，瑜謂肅曰：「昔馬援答光武云『當今之世，非但君擇臣，臣亦擇君』。

translations.literal: At that time Sun Ce had already died; Quan still dwelt at Wu; Yu said to Su, 'Formerly Ma Yuan answered Guangwu saying, "In the present generation not only does the lord choose ministers—ministers also choose the lord."'
translations.idiomatic: With Sun Ce dead and Sun Quan still at Wu, Zhou Yu quoted Ma Yuan: ministers choose their lords as well as the reverse.

sentences.zh: 今主人親賢貴士，納奇錄異，且吾聞先哲秘論，承運代劉氏者，必興於東南，推步事勢，當其歷數，終構帝基，以協天符，是烈士攀龍附鳳馳騖之秋。

translations.literal: Now the lord cherishes the worthy and esteems scholars, admits the strange and records the unusual; moreover I have heard former sages' secret discourses that he who by the mandate replaces the Liu house must rise in the southeast; pushing and stepping the situation's momentum, when its reckoning comes, in the end he will establish the imperial foundation to match Heaven's talisman—this is the autumn for a stalwart man to cling to dragon and phoenix and gallop in service.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that heaven's favor had passed southeast and Sun Quan would found an empire—time to ride the rising dragon.

sentences.zh: 吾方達此，足下不須以子揚之言介意也。

translations.literal: I am just now understanding this; you, sir, need not take Ziyang's words to heart.
translations.idiomatic: Forget Liu Ziye's letter, Zhou Yu urged—stay with the house that will win.

sentences.zh: 」肅從其言。

translations.literal: Su followed his words.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su took his advice.

sentences.zh: 瑜因薦肅才宜佐時，當廣求其比，以成功業，不可令去也。

translations.literal: Yu thereupon recommended that Su's talent was fit to assist the age; one ought broadly to seek his like to complete the enterprise—he could not be allowed to depart.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu memorialized that Lu Su must be kept and more men like him found.

sentences.zh: 權即見肅，與語甚悅之。

translations.literal: Quan immediately saw Su and in speaking with him was extremely pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan received him at once and delighted in his conversation.

sentences.zh: 眾賓罷退，肅亦辭出，乃獨引肅還，合榻對飲。

translations.literal: When the host of guests had retired, Su also took leave to go out; then alone he led Su back, shared a couch, and drank facing each other.
translations.idiomatic: When the banquet ended he drew Lu Su alone onto a shared couch for wine.

sentences.zh: 因密議曰：「今漢室傾危，四方雲擾，孤承父兄餘業，思有桓文之功。

translations.literal: Thereupon they secretly deliberated, saying, 'Now the Han house totters in peril; the four quarters swarm like clouds; the orphan inherits father and elder brother's surplus enterprise and thinks to have the achievement of Huan and Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan confided that he meant to rival Duke Huan and Duke Wen of old.

sentences.zh: 君既惠顧，何以佐之？

translations.literal: Since you, sir, have graciously looked upon me, by what will you assist me?
translations.idiomatic: He asked how Lu Su would help him.

sentences.zh: 」肅對曰：「昔高帝區區欲尊事義帝而不獲者，以項羽為害也。

translations.literal: Su answered, saying, 'Formerly the High Emperor in his meagerness wished to honor and serve Emperor Yi but could not obtain it—because Xiang Yu was the harm.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su answered that Gaozu could not serve Emperor Yi while Xiang Yu lived—

sentences.zh: 今之曹操，猶昔項羽，將軍何由得為桓文乎？

translations.literal: Today's Cao Cao is still the former Xiang Yu—by what path can the General become Huan and Wen?
translations.idiomatic: —and Cao Cao was Sun Quan's Xiang Yu, so Duke Huan's path was closed.

sentences.zh: 肅竊料之，漢室不可復興，曹操不可卒除。

translations.literal: Your servant privately reckons: the Han house cannot be revived; Cao Cao cannot be suddenly removed.
translations.idiomatic: Han could not rise again; Cao Cao could not be crushed overnight.

sentences.zh: 為將軍計，惟有鼎足江東，以觀天下之釁。

translations.literal: For the General's plan, only to tripod-foot Jiangdong and observe the realm's flaws.
translations.idiomatic: The realistic plan was to hold the southeast as one leg of a tripod and watch the north tear itself apart.

sentences.zh: 規模如此，亦自無嫌。

translations.literal: If the scale is thus, in itself there is no shame.
