translations.idiomatic: That ambition was nothing to be ashamed of.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 北方誠多務也。

translations.literal: The north truly has many tasks.
translations.idiomatic: Because the north was busy with its own troubles.

sentences.zh: 因其多務，剿除黃祖，進伐劉表，竟長江所極，據而有之，然後建號帝王以圖天下，此高帝之業也。

translations.literal: Take advantage of its many tasks—wipe out Huang Zu, advance and punish Liu Biao, exhaust the Long River's utmost, hold and possess it; then establish the title emperor-king and plan the realm—this is the High Emperor's enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Strike Huang Zu, take Liu Biao, hold the whole Yangzi, then declare kingship—Gaozu's own playbook.

sentences.zh: 」權曰：「今盡力方冀以輔漢耳，此言非所及也。

translations.literal: Quan said, 'Now with full strength I only hope thereby to assist Han—this talk is not what I can reach.'
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan protested that he only meant to aid Han, not usurp it.

sentences.zh: 」張昭非肅謙下不足，頗訾毀之，云肅年少粗疏，未可用。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhao criticized Su for insufficient modesty below, quite slandered him, saying Su was young and crude and not yet usable.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao called Lu Su brash and unusable.

sentences.zh: 極不以介意，益貴重之，賜肅母衣服幃帳，居處雜物，富擬其舊。

translations.literal: Quan extremely did not take it to heart, all the more prized and honored him, gave Su's mother clothes, curtains, bedding, dwelling miscellany—wealth rivaling the old.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan ignored the slander, heaped gifts on Lu Su's mother, and prized him the more.

sentences.zh: 劉表死，肅進說曰：「夫荊楚與國鄰接，水流順北，外帶江漢，內阻山陵，有金城之固，沃野萬里，士民殷富，若據而有之，此帝王之資也。

translations.literal: When Liu Biao died, Su advanced counsel, saying, 'Jing-Chu borders our state; its waters flow smoothly north; outward it belts the Jiang and Han, inward it blocks mountains and hills—it has the firmness of metal walls, fertile wilds ten thousand li, gentry and people abundant and rich; if we seize and hold it, this is capital for an emperor-king.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Biao died Lu Su urged that Jingzhou—river, mountains, wealth—was the stuff of empire.

sentences.zh: 今表新亡，二子素不輯睦，軍中諸將，各有彼此。

translations.literal: Now Biao is newly dead; the two sons by nature are not harmonious; among the army's generals each has his own faction.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao's sons quarreled; his generals split into factions.

sentences.zh: 加劉備天下梟雄，與操有隙，寄寓於表，表惡其能而不能用也。

translations.literal: Add Liu Bei, fierce raptor of the realm, at odds with Cao, lodging with Biao—Biao hated his ability and could not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei, Cao Cao's foe, was stranded under a jealous Liu Biao.

sentences.zh: 若備與彼協心，上下齊同，則宜撫安，與結盟好：如有離違，宜別圖之，以濟大事。

translations.literal: If Bei joins hearts with them, above and below uniform, then it is fitting to soothe and settle them and ally in good faith; if there is separation and violation, it is fitting to plan otherwise for them, to aid the great affair.
translations.idiomatic: If Liu Bei joins Liu's heirs, befriend them; if they split, exploit the breach for Wu's gain.

sentences.zh: 肅請得奉命吊表二子，並慰勞其軍中用事者，及說備使撫表眾，同心一意，共治曹操，備必喜而從命。

translations.literal: Su begs to receive mandate to condole Biao's two sons and also comfort the army's men in charge of affairs, and persuade Bei to soothe Biao's host, one heart one intent, jointly governing Cao Cao—Bei is sure to be pleased and follow orders.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su asked leave to mourn Liu's sons, woo Liu Bei's men, and weld them against Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 如其克諧，天下可定也。

translations.literal: If it can be harmonized, the realm can be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Success would settle the empire.

sentences.zh: 今不速往，恐為操所先。

translations.literal: If we do not go swiftly, I fear Cao will be first.
translations.idiomatic: Delay would let Cao Cao strike first.

sentences.zh: 」權即遣肅行。

translations.literal: Quan immediately sent Su on the mission.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan sent him at once.

sentences.zh: 到夏口，聞曹公已向荊州，晨夜兼道。

translations.literal: Arriving at Xiakou, he heard Lord Cao had already gone toward Jingzhou; he traveled day and night.
translations.idiomatic: He raced to Xiakou, heard Cao Cao was moving on Jingzhou, and doubled his pace.

sentences.zh: 比至南郡，而表子琮已降曹公，備惶遽奔走，欲南渡江。

translations.literal: By the time he reached Nan commandery, Biao's son Cong had already surrendered to Lord Cao; Bei fled in alarm, wishing to cross south of the river.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Nan commandery too late—Liu Cong had surrendered and Liu Bei was bolting south.

sentences.zh: 肅徑迎之，到當陽長阪，與備會，宣騰權旨，及陳江東強固，勸備與權並力。

translations.literal: Su went straight to meet him; arriving at Changban of Dangyang he met Bei, proclaimed and raised Quan's intent, and set forth how the eastern river was strong and firm, urging Bei to join strength with Quan.
translations.idiomatic: He intercepted Liu Bei at Changban, delivered Sun Quan's offer, and pressed an alliance.

sentences.zh: 備甚歡悅。

translations.literal: Bei was extremely pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 時諸葛亮與備相隨。

translations.literal: At that time Zhuge Liang accompanied Bei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang was with him.

sentences.zh: 肅謂亮曰「我子瑜友也」，即共定交。

translations.literal: Su said to Liang, 'I am Ziyu's friend,' and immediately together they fixed friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su told Zhuge Liang they were both friends of Zhuge Jin and sealed friendship on the spot.

sentences.zh: 備遂到夏口，遣亮使權，肅亦反命。

translations.literal: Bei thereupon reached Xiakou, sent Liang as envoy to Quan; Su also returned with his report.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei reached Xiakou, sent Zhuge Liang to Sun Quan, and Lu Su rode back with his answer.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案：劉備與權並力，共拒中國，皆肅之本謀。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi notes: Liu Bei and Quan joined strength jointly to resist the central state—all was Su's original plan.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi insists the Liu-Sun alliance was Lu Su's design from the start.

sentences.zh: 又語諸葛亮曰「我子瑜友也」，則亮已亟聞肅言矣。

translations.literal: Again he spoke to Zhuge Liang saying, 'I am Ziyu's friend'—then Liang had already repeatedly heard Su's words.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su's claim to be Zhuge Jin's friend meant Zhuge Liang had heard his pitch before.

sentences.zh: 而《蜀書亮傳》曰：「亮以連橫之略說權，權乃大喜。

translations.literal: Yet the Shu shu, Liang's biography, states: 'Liang with the horizontal-alliance stratagem persuaded Quan, and Quan was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Yet *Shu Records* credits Zhuge Liang's horizontal-alliance speech for Sun Quan's joy—

sentences.zh: 」如似此計始出於亮。

translations.literal: As if this plan first issued from Liang.
translations.idiomatic: —as if the idea began with Zhuge Liang alone.

sentences.zh: 若二國史官，各記所聞，競欲稱揚本國容美，各取其功。

translations.literal: If the two states' scribes each record what they heard, competing to praise their state's appearance and beauty, each taking its own merit—
translations.idiomatic: When two courts each glorify their own heroes—

sentences.zh: 今此二書，同出一人，而舛互若此，非載述之體也。〉

translations.literal: now these two books issue from one man yet contradict thus—it is not the body of recording.〉
translations.idiomatic: —Pei marvels that one author could contradict himself so grossly.〉

sentences.zh: 會權得曹公欲東之問，與諸將議，皆勸權迎之，而肅獨不言。

translations.literal: It happened that Quan obtained news that Lord Cao wished to go east; deliberating with the generals, all urged Quan to welcome him, while Su alone did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao threatened invasion the council urged surrender; Lu Su alone stayed silent.

sentences.zh: 權起更衣，肅追於宇下，權知其意，執肅手曰：「卿欲何言？

translations.literal: Quan rose to change clothes; Su pursued beneath the eaves; Quan knew his intent, grasped Su's hand, and said, 'What do you wish to say?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan stepped out to change; Lu Su followed; Sun Quan caught his hand and asked his mind.

sentences.zh: 」肅對曰：「向察眾人之議，專欲誤將軍，不足與圖大事。

translations.literal: Su answered, 'Just now observing the multitude's discussion, they only wish to mislead the General—not sufficient to plan great affairs with.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su said the courtiers would ruin him—

sentences.zh: 今肅可迎操耳，如將軍，不可也。

translations.literal: Now Su could welcome Cao; as for the General, it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: —he could surrender; Sun Quan could not.

sentences.zh: 何以言之？

translations.literal: By what is it spoken?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 今肅迎操，操當以肅還付鄉黨。

translations.literal: Now if Su welcomes Cao, Cao ought to return Su to his village party.
translations.idiomatic: If he surrendered, Cao Cao would pack him home to his county.

sentences.zh: 品其名位，猶不失下曹從事，乘犢車、從吏卒、交遊士林、累官故不失州郡也。

translations.literal: Evaluating his name and rank, still he would not miss being a lower-bureau clerk, riding a calf cart, following clerk soldiers, consorting with the forest of scholars, piling office after office—still he would not miss a province or commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He might still rate a minor clerkship, ride a cart, rise to provincial office—life would go on.

sentences.zh: 將軍迎操，欲安所歸？

translations.literal: If the General welcomes Cao, where do you intend to return?
translations.idiomatic: If you surrender to Cao Cao, where will you yourself end up?

sentences.zh: 願早定大計，莫用眾人之議也。

translations.literal: I pray you settle the great plan early; do not use the multitude's discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Settle the great decision now—do not follow the cowards.

sentences.zh: 」權歎息曰：「此諸人持議，甚失孤望；

translations.literal: Quan sighed and said, 'These men's holding the discussion has greatly missed what the orphan hoped;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan sighed that the council had disappointed him—

sentences.zh: 今卿廓開大計，正與孤同，此天以卿賜我也。」

translations.literal: now you, sir, have opened wide the great plan, exactly matching the orphan's mind—this is Heaven giving you to me.'
translations.idiomatic: —but Lu Su's counsel matched his own: Heaven had sent him Lu Su.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》及《九州春秋》曰：曹公徵荊州，孫權大懼，魯肅實欲勸權拒曹公，乃激說權曰：「彼曹公者，實嚴敵也，新並袁紹，兵馬甚精，乘戰勝之威，伐喪亂之國，克可必也。

translations.literal: The Wei shu and Jiuzhou chunqiu state: When Lord Cao campaigned against Jingzhou, Sun Quan was greatly afraid; Lu Su in truth wished to urge Quan to resist Lord Cao, therefore provocatively said to Quan, 'That Lord Cao is in truth a stern foe; he has newly annexed Yuan Shao, his soldiers and horses are extremely keen, riding the awe of victory to attack a state in mourning and chaos—victory can be certain.
translations.idiomatic: A hostile Wei tradition claims Lu Su frightened Sun Quan with Cao's strength—

sentences.zh: 不如遣兵助之，且送將軍家詣鄴；

translations.literal: Better send troops to aid him and moreover escort the General's household to Ye;
translations.idiomatic: —and urged sending troops to help Cao Cao and shipping Sun Quan's family to Ye—

sentences.zh: 不然，將危。

translations.literal: if not, there will be peril.
translations.idiomatic: —or face ruin.

sentences.zh: 」權大怒，欲斬肅，肅因曰：「今事已急，即有他圖，何不遣兵助劉備，而欲斬我乎？

translations.literal: Quan was greatly angry and wished to behead Su; Su thereupon said, 'Now the affair is already urgent—if there is another plan, why not send troops to aid Liu Bei, yet you wish to behead me?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan feigned rage; Lu Su retorted that beheading him would not save the situation.

sentences.zh: 」權然之，乃遣周瑜助備。

translations.literal: Quan approved it and thereupon sent Zhou Yu to aid Bei.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan agreed and sent Zhou Yu to reinforce Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 孫盛曰：吳書及江表傳，魯肅一見孫權便說拒曹公而論帝王之略，劉表之死也，又請使觀變，無緣方復激說勸迎曹公也。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng says: The Wu shu and Jiang biao zhuan have Lu Su on first seeing Sun Quan already speak of resisting Lord Cao and discoursing the emperor-king's strategy; at Liu Biao's death he again asked to be sent to observe change—there was no reason then again provocatively to urge welcoming Lord Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng rejects the Wei tale: Lu Su had always argued for resistance.

sentences.zh: 又是時勸迎者眾，而云獨欲斬肅，非其論也。〉

translations.literal: Moreover at that time those who urged welcoming were many—yet it says he alone wished to behead Su—not its argument.〉
translations.idiomatic: Many had urged surrender; the story that only Lu Su faced execution is absurd.〉

sentences.zh: 時周瑜受使至鄱陽，肅勸追召瑜還。

translations.literal: At that time Zhou Yu had received mission and reached Poyang; Su urged pursuing summons to recall Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su had Zhou Yu recalled from Poyang.

sentences.zh: 遂任瑜以行事，以肅為贊軍校尉，助畫方略。

translations.literal: Thereupon he entrusted Yu with conducting affairs, made Su Colonel Who Supports the Army, assisting in planning strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan gave Zhou Yu command and named Lu Su colonel who supports the army to help plan the campaign.

sentences.zh: 曹公破走，肅即先還，權大請諸將迎肅。

translations.literal: When Lord Cao was broken and put to flight, Su returned first; Quan greatly summoned the generals to welcome Su.
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Cao's rout Lu Su came back first; Sun Quan mustered the generals to greet him.

sentences.zh: 肅將入閣拜，權起禮之，因謂曰：「子敬，孤持鞍下馬相迎，足以顯卿未？

translations.literal: When Su was about to enter the chamber to bow, Quan rose and saluted him, thereupon saying, 'Zijing, the orphan holding the saddle and dismounting the horse to welcome you—is it enough to display you?'
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan dismounted to meet him and asked if that honor sufficed.

sentences.zh: 」肅趨近曰：「未也。

translations.literal: Su hurried forward and said, 'Not yet.'
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su answered, 'Not yet.'

sentences.zh: 」眾人聞之，無不愕然。

translations.literal: When the host heard it, none was not stunned.
translations.idiomatic: The court gasped.

sentences.zh: 就坐，徐舉鞭言曰：「願至尊威德加乎四海。

translations.literal: When seated, slowly raising his whip he said, 'I hope the Exalted One's awe and virtue may extend over the four seas;
translations.idiomatic: Seated, he raised his whip: true glory would come when—

sentences.zh: 總括九州，克成帝業，更以安車軟輪徵肅，始當顯耳。

translations.literal: gathering in the Nine Provinces, completing the imperial enterprise, then with cushioned cart and soft wheels summoning Su—that will be display enough.'
translations.idiomatic: —Sun Quan ruled all under Heaven and summoned him with the carriage reserved for the highest ministers.

sentences.zh: 」權撫掌歡笑。

translations.literal: Quan clapped his hands and laughed joyfully.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan roared with laughter.

sentences.zh: 後備詣京見權，求都督荊州，惟肅勸權借之，共拒曹公。

translations.literal: Later when Bei went to the capital to see Quan, seeking to be area commander of Jingzhou, only Su urged Quan to lend it, jointly resisting Lord Cao.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei asked to govern Jingzhou, only Lu Su urged Sun Quan to lend him the land against Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 〈《漢晉春秋》曰：呂範勸留備，肅曰：「不可。

translations.literal: The Han-Jin chunqiu states: Lü Fan urged detaining Bei; Su said, 'It cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: The *Han-Jin chunqiu* says Lü Fan wanted to hold Liu Bei; Lu Su refused—

sentences.zh: 將軍雖神武命世，然曹公威力實重，初臨荊州，恩信未洽，宜以藉備，使撫安之。

translations.literal: Though the General is divinely martial and commands the age, yet Lord Cao's might and power are truly weighty; having first come to Jingzhou, favor and trust are not yet harmonized—it is fitting thereby to lend to Bei and have him soothe and settle it.
translations.idiomatic: —Cao Cao still threatened the north; lending Jingzhou to Liu Bei would win a buffer and a shield.

sentences.zh: 多操之敵，而自為樹黨，計之上也。

translations.literal: Increasing Lord Cao's enemies and for yourself planting a party—this is the top of stratagems.'
translations.idiomatic: More enemies for Cao Cao and an ally for Wu was the best policy.

sentences.zh: 」權即從之。〉

translations.literal: Quan immediately followed it.〉
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan agreed.〉

sentences.zh: 曹公聞權以土地業備，方作書，落筆於地。

translations.literal: When Lord Cao heard that Quan with land enriched Bei, he was just writing a letter when the brush fell to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao heard Sun Quan had ceded land to Liu Bei, his brush dropped from his hand.

sentences.zh: 周瑜病困，上疏曰：「當今天下，方有事役，是瑜乃心夙夜所憂，願至尊先慮未然，然後康樂。

translations.literal: Zhou Yu gravely ill submitted a memorial saying, 'Now under heaven there are just then military corvees—this is what Yu's heart night and day worries; I hope the Exalted One will first consider what is not yet so, then afterward enjoy peace and joy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu's deathbed memorial urged Sun Quan to plan for danger before feasting.

sentences.zh: 今既與曹操為敵，劉備近在公安，邊境密邇，百姓未附，宜得良將以鎮撫之。

translations.literal: Now already enemies with Cao Cao, Liu Bei lodges close at Gong'an—the border is near, the hundred surnames not yet attached—it is fitting to obtain a good general to guard and soothe them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei at Gong'an needed a strong hand on the border.

sentences.zh: 魯肅智略足任，乞以代瑜。

translations.literal: Lu Su's wisdom and strategy are sufficient for the post; I beg to use him to replace Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He nominated Lu Su to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 瑜隕踣之日，所懷盡矣。」

translations.literal: On the day Yu falls and stumbles, what I harbored is exhausted.'
translations.idiomatic: With his fall, he said, his mind's burden was spent.

sentences.zh: 〈《江表傳》載：初瑜疾困，與權箋曰：「瑜以凡才，昔受討逆殊特之遇，委以腹心，遂荷榮任，統御兵馬，志執鞭弭，自效戎行。

translations.literal: The Jiang biao zhuan records: When Yu first was gravely ill he wrote Quan a note saying, 'Yu with ordinary talent formerly received the campaign-general's extraordinary favor, was entrusted as heart and liver, thereupon bore glorious office, commanding and controlling soldiers and horses, resolved to grasp whip and dust-wiper and offer service in the army ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The *Jiangbiao zhuan* gives Zhou Yu's longer farewell letter to Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 規定巴蜀，次取襄陽，憑賴威靈，謂若在握。

translations.literal: Planned to settle Ba-Shu, next take Xiangyang, relying on awesome spirit—thought it as if in the grasp.
translations.idiomatic: He had meant to take Ba-Shu, then Xiangyang, confident of success.

sentences.zh: 至以不謹，道遇暴疾，昨自醫療，日加無損。

translations.literal: Until through lack of caution on the road I met a sudden illness; yesterday I treated myself, daily increasing without improvement.
translations.idiomatic: A sudden illness had laid him low despite treatment.

sentences.zh: 人生有死，修短命矣，誠不足惜，但恨微志未展，不復奉教命耳。

translations.literal: Human life has death; short or long span—truly not worth regretting; only I hate that my slight aim was not unfolded, no longer to receive your teaching and orders.
translations.idiomatic: Death was nothing; only unfinished duty pained him.

sentences.zh: 方今曹公在北，疆埸未靜，劉備寄寓，有似養虎，天下之事，未知終始，此朝士旰食之秋，至尊垂慮之日也。

translations.literal: Now Cao Cao is in the north, the border not yet quiet, Liu Bei lodged with us like raising a tiger—affairs under heaven's end and beginning are not yet known; this is the autumn when court gentlemen forget to eat, the day when the Exalted One should let care hang down.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao still threatened north; Liu Bei was a tiger in the house—Sun Quan must stay vigilant.

sentences.zh: 魯肅忠烈，臨事不苟，可以代瑜。

translations.literal: Lu Su is loyal and fierce, facing affairs not careless—he can replace Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su was loyal, careful, and fit to replace him.

sentences.zh: 人之將死，其言也善，儻或可採，瑜死不朽矣。

translations.literal: When a man is about to die, his words are good—if perhaps they can be taken, Yu's death will not decay.
translations.idiomatic: The dying speak truth; if Sun Quan heeded him, his death would not be vain.

sentences.zh: 」案此箋與本傳所載，意旨雖同，其辭乖異耳。〉

translations.literal: Note: this note and what the main biography records—though the intent is the same, the wording diverges.〉
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes wording differs between letter and biography.〉

sentences.zh: 即拜肅奮武校尉，代瑜領兵。

translations.literal: Immediately he appointed Su Colonel Who Rouses Might, replacing Yu in leading troops.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan at once named Lu Su colonel who rouses might and gave him Zhou Yu's command.

sentences.zh: 瑜士眾四千餘人。

translations.literal: Yu's soldiers and masses were more than four thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited more than four thousand of Zhou Yu's men.

sentences.zh: 奉邑四縣，皆屬焉。

translations.literal: The four counties of fief income all belonged to him.
translations.idiomatic: The four revenue counties went with the post.

sentences.zh: 令程普領南郡太守。

translations.literal: He ordered Cheng Pu to lead Administrator of Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Pu was named governor of Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 肅初住江陵，後下屯陸口，威恩大行，眾增萬餘人，拜漢昌太守、偏將軍。

translations.literal: Su at first dwelt at Jiangling, later moved down to encamp at Lukou; awe and favor ran greatly; the host increased by more than ten thousand; he was appointed Administrator of Hanchang and Lieutenant General.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su began at Jiangling, moved to Lukou, swelled his army past ten thousand, and rose to governor of Hanchang and lieutenant general.

sentences.zh: 十九年，從權破皖城，轉橫江將軍。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he followed Quan in breaking Wan city and was transferred General Who Crosses the River.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he helped take Wan and became general who crosses the river.

sentences.zh: 先是，益州牧劉璋綱維頹弛。

translations.literal: Before this, Shepherd of Yi Province Liu Zhang's net and cable were slack and dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liu Zhang's grip on Yi Province had slackened.

sentences.zh: 周瑜、甘寧並勸權取蜀，權以諮備，備內欲自規。

translations.literal: Zhou Yu and Gan Ning together urged Quan to take Shu; Quan consulted Bei; Bei inwardly wished to plan for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu and Gan Ning urged an attack on Shu; Sun Quan asked Liu Bei, who secretly meant to take it himself.

sentences.zh: 仍偽報曰：「備與璋托為宗室，冀憑英靈，以匡漢朝。

translations.literal: Still falsely replying, he said, 'Bei and Zhang, entrusting ourselves as imperial clan, hope relying on heroic spirits to aid the Han house.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei lied that he and Liu Zhang, as kinsmen of Han, meant to help the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 今璋得罪左右，備獨竦懼，非所敢聞，願加寬貸。

translations.literal: Now Zhang has offended those about you; Bei alone stands in fear—this is not what I dare hear; I beg indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded for mercy for Liu Zhang.

sentences.zh: 若不獲請，備當放發歸於山林。

translations.literal: If the request is not obtained, Bei ought to let down hair and return to mountain and forest.'
translations.idiomatic: If refused, he would retire to the hills.

sentences.zh: 」後備西圖璋，留關羽守。

translations.literal: Later Bei plotted west against Zhang, leaving Guan Yu to guard.
translations.idiomatic: Then Liu Bei marched west on Liu Zhang and left Guan Yu.

sentences.zh: 權曰：「猾虜乃敢挾詐！

translations.literal: Quan said, 'The cunning captive dares carry fraud!'
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan snarled that the rogue had tricked him.

sentences.zh: 」及羽與肅鄰界，數生​​狐疑，疆場紛錯，肅常以歡好撫之。

translations.literal: When Yu bordered Su, repeatedly life brought doubt; the border field was tangled and wrong—Su always used good cheer to soothe it.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu and Lu Su shared a tense border; Lu Su kept smoothing friction.

sentences.zh: 備既定益州，權求長沙、零、桂，備不承旨，權遣呂蒙率眾近取。

translations.literal: When Bei had settled Yi Province, Quan sought Changsha, Ling, and Gui; Bei did not accept the decree; Quan sent Lü Meng leading the host to take them by approach.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Bei took Yi, Sun Quan demanded southern commanderies; refused, he sent Lü Meng.

sentences.zh: 備聞，自還公安，遣羽爭三郡。

translations.literal: When Bei heard, he himself returned to Gong'an and sent Yu to contest the three commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei rushed back to Gong'an and sent Guan Yu to fight for the three districts.

sentences.zh: 肅住益陽，與羽相拒。

translations.literal: Su dwelt at Yiyang, opposing Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su camped at Yiyang opposite Guan Yu.

sentences.zh: 肅邀羽相見，各駐兵馬百步上，但諸將軍單刀俱會。

translations.literal: Su invited Yu to meet; each stationed horse and army a hundred paces above, but the generals with single blades all attended together.
translations.idiomatic: He invited Guan Yu to a parley with armies halted a hundred paces off—generals only, swords in hand.

sentences.zh: 肅因責數羽曰：「國家區區本以土地借卿家者，卿家軍敗遠來，無以為資故也。

translations.literal: Su thereupon reproached Yu, saying, 'The state in its meagerness originally lent land to your house because your house's army was defeated and came from afar, having nothing to serve as resource.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su rebuked Guan Yu: Wu had lent land because Liu Bei arrived broken and destitute.

sentences.zh: 今已得益州，既無奉還之意，但求三郡，又不從命。

translations.literal: Now having obtained Yi Province, there is no intent to return favor; only seeking three commanderies, again you do not follow orders.'
translations.idiomatic: Now enriched by Yi, Liu Bei would not return even three commanderies.

sentences.zh: 」語未究竟，坐有一人曰：「夫土地者，惟德所在耳，何常之有！

translations.literal: Before the words were finished, one sitting there said, 'As for land, only where virtue dwells—what constancy is there!'
translations.idiomatic: Before he finished, someone shouted that land belongs to virtue alone.

sentences.zh: 」肅厲聲呵之，辭色甚切。

translations.literal: Su in a stern voice shouted at him; words and color were very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su shouted him down sharply.

sentences.zh: 羽操刀起謂曰：「此自國家事，是人何知！

translations.literal: Yu grasped his knife, rose, and said, 'This is itself the state's affair—how can this fellow know!'
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu gripped his blade: state business was not for underlings.

sentences.zh: 」目使之去。

translations.literal: His eyes made him go away.
translations.idiomatic: He glared the man away.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：肅欲與羽會語，諸將疑恐有變，議不可往。

translations.literal: The Wu shu states: When Su wished to meet Yu in talk, the generals doubted and feared there might be change; they deliberated that he could not go.
translations.idiomatic: The *Wu shu* says the generals feared a trap.

sentences.zh: 肅曰：「今日之事，宜相開譬。

translations.literal: Su said, 'Today's affair ought mutually to open and explain.'
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su insisted the meeting must clarify matters.

sentences.zh: 劉備負國，是非未決，羽亦何敢重欲幹命！

translations.literal: Liu Bei has betrayed the state; right and wrong are not yet decided—how dare Yu heavily wish to usurp command!'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei's loyalty was still in question—Guan Yu could not dictate terms.

sentences.zh: 」乃趨就羽。

translations.literal: Thereupon he hastened to approach Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He walked straight to Guan Yu.

sentences.zh: 羽曰：「烏林之役，左將軍身在行間，寢不脫介，戮力破魏，豈得徒勞，無一塊壤，而足下來欲收地邪？

translations.literal: Yu said, 'In the Wulin campaign the General of the Left was personally in the ranks, slept without removing armor, joined strength to break Wei—how can it be vain toil, not one clod of soil, yet you, sir, come wishing to take back land?'
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu retorted that Liu Bei had fought at Wulin without stripping his mail—why owe land?

sentences.zh: 」肅曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Su said, 'Not so.'
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su answered, 'Not so.'

sentences.zh: 始與豫州觀於長阪，豫州之眾不當一校，計窮慮極，志勢摧弱，圖欲遠竄，望不及此。

translations.literal: At first I with the Governor of Yu Province met at Changban; the Governor of Yu Province's host was not equal to one school; plans exhausted and cares at the end, intent and momentum crushed and weak, he plotted wishing to flee far—he did not hope to reach this.
translations.idiomatic: At Changban Liu Bei's men were fewer than a single regiment—he meant only to run, not to rule Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 主上矜愍豫州之身，無有處所，不愛土地士人之力，使有所庇廕以濟其患，而豫州私獨飾情，愆德隳好。

translations.literal: Our lord pitied the Governor of Yu Province's person, having no place to dwell, not sparing land and the strength of gentry and people, letting him have shelter to relieve his calamity—yet the Governor of Yu Province alone adorned feeling in private, defaulted on virtue and ruined the good.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan pitied him and gave shelter; Liu Bei repaid kindness with treachery.

sentences.zh: 今已藉手於西州矣，又欲翦並荊州之土，斯蓋凡夫所不忍行，而況整領人物之主乎！

translations.literal: Now already having borrowed a hand in the western province, again wishing to clip and annex Jingzhou's soil—this is what even a common fellow cannot bear to do, how much more a lord who orders and leads the host of men!'
translations.idiomatic: Having seized the west he now wanted to swallow Jingzhou—no honorable man would do it.

sentences.zh: 肅聞貪而棄義，必為禍階。

translations.literal: Su has heard that greed which casts aside righteousness must become the step of calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Greed that scorns right invites disaster.

sentences.zh: 吾子屬當重任，曾不能明道處分，以義輔時，而負恃弱眾以圖力爭，師曲為老，將何獲濟？

translations.literal: You, sir, belong to bearing heavy responsibility—how can you fail to clarify the Way and dispose affairs, with righteousness assisting the times, yet rely on a weak host to plan forceful struggle? When the army is crooked it grows old—what will you obtain to succeed?'
translations.idiomatic: A general who leans on might without justice marches to defeat—what gain is there?

sentences.zh: 」羽無以答。〉

translations.literal: Yu had nothing to answer.〉
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu had no reply.〉

sentences.zh: 備遂割湘水為界，於是罷軍。

translations.literal: Bei thereupon cut the Xiang River as boundary; thereupon the armies were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei then split territory at the Xiang River and both sides stood down.

sentences.zh: 肅年四十六，建安二十二年卒。

translations.literal: Su's years were forty-six; in the twenty-second year of Jian'an he died.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su died at forty-six in Jian'an 22 (217 CE).

sentences.zh: 權為舉哀，又臨其葬。

translations.literal: Quan for him raised mourning and again attended his burial.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan mourned him and attended his funeral.

sentences.zh: 諸葛亮亦為發哀。

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang also for him raised mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang mourned him as well.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：肅為人方嚴，寡於玩飾，內外節儉，不務俗好。

translations.literal: The Wu shu states: Su as a man was square and stern, spare in play and adornment, inward and outward frugal, not pursuing vulgar likes.
translations.idiomatic: The *Book of Wu* calls him stern, austere, and indifferent to luxury.

sentences.zh: 治軍整頓，禁令必行，雖在軍陳，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: He ordered the army neat and firm; prohibitions and orders were sure to be executed; though in army formation, his hand did not release the scroll.
translations.idiomatic: His camps were disciplined; even in the field he kept a book in hand.

sentences.zh: 又善談論，能屬文辭，思度弘遠，有過人之明。

translations.literal: Again he was good at discourse, able to compose literary phrasing; thought and measure broad and far—he had brightness surpassing others.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke and wrote well, with vision beyond ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 周瑜之後，肅為之冠。〉

translations.literal: After Zhou Yu, Su was chief among them.〉
translations.idiomatic: After Zhou Yu's death he stood first among Wu's strategists.〉

sentences.zh: 權稱尊號，臨壇，願謂公卿曰：「昔魯子敬嘗道此，可謂明於事勢矣。

translations.literal: When Quan assumed the imperial title, approaching the altar, he looked toward the Excellencies and ministers and said, 'Formerly Lu Zijing once spoke of this—it can be called clear in the situation's momentum.'
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan took the throne he told his court Lu Su had foreseen it.

sentences.zh: 」肅遣腹子淑既壯，濡須督張承謂終當到至。

translations.literal: Su left a posthumous son Shu; when he had grown to maturity, Zhang Cheng, commander at Ruxu, said he would in the end reach the top.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su's posthumous son Lu Shu grew up; Zhang Cheng at Ruxu predicted he would rise high.

sentences.zh: 永安中，為昭武將軍、都亭侯、武昌督。

translations.literal: In the Yongan period he was General Who Displays Martial Might, Marquis of Duting village, commander of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongan era he became general who displays martial might, village marquis of Duting, and Wuchang commander.

sentences.zh: 建衡中，假節，遷夏口督。

translations.literal: In the Jianheng period he was granted the tally and transferred commander of Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jianheng he received the imperial tally and moved to command Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 所在嚴整，有方乾。

translations.literal: Wherever he was, strict and ordered, he had method and backbone.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he ran a tight camp with clear judgment.

sentences.zh: 鳳皇三年卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Fenghuang he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Fenghuang 3.

sentences.zh: 子睦襲爵，領兵馬。

translations.literal: His son Mu inherited the rank and led soldiers and horses.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lu Mu inherited the title and commanded troops.

sentences.zh: 呂蒙字子明，汝南富陂人也。

translations.literal: Lü Meng, courtesy name Ziming, was a man of Fupo in Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng, courtesy Ziming, came from Fupo in Runan.

sentences.zh: 少南渡，依姊夫鄧當。

translations.literal: In youth he crossed south and relied on his brother-in-law Deng Dang.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he crossed south to his brother-in-law Deng Dang.

sentences.zh: 當為孫策將，數討山越。

translations.literal: Dang was a general of Sun Ce and repeatedly campaigned against the mountain Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Dang served Sun Ce against the hill tribes.

sentences.zh: 蒙年十五六，竊隨當擊賊，當顧見大驚，呵叱不能禁止。

translations.literal: Meng at age fifteen or sixteen secretly followed Dang in striking bandits; Dang looked and saw, was greatly startled, shouted and scolded but could not stop him.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen Lü Meng followed Deng Dang into battle; Deng Dang could not stop him.

sentences.zh: 歸以告蒙母，母恚欲罰之，蒙曰：「貧賤難可居，脫誤有功，富貴可致。

translations.literal: Returning he told Meng's mother; the mother was angry and wished to punish him; Meng said, 'Poverty and lowliness are hard to dwell in; if by chance there is merit, riches and honor can be reached.
translations.idiomatic: His mother meant to punish him; he said poverty was unbearable and merit could win wealth.

sentences.zh: 旦不探虎穴，安得虎子？

translations.literal: Moreover if one does not enter the tiger's den, how can one obtain the tiger cub?'
translations.idiomatic: How catch tiger cubs without entering the den?

sentences.zh: 」母哀而捨之。

translations.literal: The mother pitied him and let him off.
translations.idiomatic: She relented.

sentences.zh: 時當職吏以蒙年小輕之，曰：「彼堅子何能為？

translations.literal: At that time Dang's duty clerk because Meng was young belittled him, saying, 'What can that stubborn boy do?
translations.idiomatic: A petty officer sneered at the boy soldier—

sentences.zh: 此欲以肉餧虎耳。

translations.literal: This wants to feed meat to a tiger's ears.'
translations.idiomatic: —calling him meat for tigers.

sentences.zh: 」他日與蒙會，又蚩辱之。

translations.literal: Another day he met with Meng and again sneered and insulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Later the same clerk mocked him again.

sentences.zh: 蒙大怒，引刀殺吏，出走，逃邑子鄭長家。

translations.literal: Meng was greatly angry, drew a knife and killed the clerk, ran out, fled to his townsman Zheng Chang's house.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng drew his knife, killed the clerk, and fled to a neighbor's house.

sentences.zh: 出因校尉袁雄自首，承間為言，策召見奇之，引置左右。

translations.literal: Going out he thereupon through Colonel Yuan Xiong gave himself up; taking advantage of a gap Xiong spoke for him; Ce summoned and saw him, thought him extraordinary, and led him to attend at his side.
translations.idiomatic: He surrendered through Colonel Yuan Xiong; Sun Ce met him, saw his mettle, and kept him at headquarters.

sentences.zh: 數歲，鄧當死，張昭薦蒙代當，拜別部司馬。

translations.literal: After several years Deng Dang died; Zhang Zhao recommended Meng to replace Dang; he was appointed Major of a Separate Department.
translations.idiomatic: When Deng Dang died, Zhang Zhao recommended Lü Meng as his successor as major of a separate command.

sentences.zh: 權統事，料諸小將兵少而用薄者，欲併合之。

translations.literal: When Quan took charge of affairs, he assessed the minor generals whose troops were few and use thin—he wished to merge them.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan planned to merge small undermanned commands.

sentences.zh: 蒙陰賒貰，為兵作絳衣行滕，及簡日，陳列赫然，兵人練習，權見之大悅，增其兵。

translations.literal: Meng secretly borrowed on credit, for the soldiers made crimson clothes and marching leggings; on review day the display was splendid, the soldiers drilled and practiced; Quan saw it and was greatly pleased, increased his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng borrowed money to dress his men in red uniforms for inspection; Sun Quan was delighted and enlarged his command.

sentences.zh: 從討丹楊，所向有功，拜平北都尉，領廣德長。

translations.literal: He followed in punishing Danyang; wherever faced he had merit; was appointed Colonel Who Pacifies the North, heading as magistrate of Guangde.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned in Danyang, won honors, and became colonel who pacifies the north and magistrate of Guangde.

sentences.zh: 從徵黃祖，祖令都督陳就逆以水軍出戰。

translations.literal: He followed in campaigning against Huang Zu; Zu ordered area commander Chen Jiu to oppose with the navy and come out to battle.
translations.idiomatic: Against Huang Zu, Chen Jiu led the river fleet out to fight.

sentences.zh: 蒙勒前鋒，親梟就首，將士乘勝，進攻其城。

translations.literal: Meng drove the van, personally beheaded Jiu's head; officers and soldiers rode victory and advanced to attack the city.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng led the van and cut off Chen Jiu's head; his men pressed the assault.

sentences.zh: 祖聞就死，委城走，兵追禽之。

translations.literal: When Zu heard Jiu was dead, he abandoned the city and fled; troops pursued and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zu fled; they ran him down and took him.

sentences.zh: 權曰：「事之克，由陳就先獲也。

translations.literal: Quan said, 'The affair's success came from Chen Jiu being taken first.'
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan said victory began with Chen Jiu's death.

sentences.zh: 」以蒙為橫野中郎將，賜錢千萬。

translations.literal: He appointed Meng Colonel of the Wilds Who Crosses the Field and gave cash in the tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: He named Lü Meng colonel of the wilds who crosses the field and paid him a fortune in cash.

sentences.zh: 是歲，又與周瑜、程普等西破曹公於烏林，圍曹仁於南郡。

translations.literal: That year again together with Zhou Yu, Cheng Pu, and others he broke Lord Cao west at Wulin and besieged Cao Ren in Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: That year he joined Zhou Yu and Cheng Pu to defeat Cao Cao at Wulin and besiege Cao Ren in Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 益州將襲肅舉軍來附，瑜表以肅兵益蒙，蒙盛稱肅有膽用。

translations.literal: Yi Province's general Xi Su raised the whole army to come attach; Yu memorialized to add Su's troops to Meng; Meng greatly praised Su for courage and usefulness.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Su of Yi defected with his army; Zhou Yu gave his men to Lü Meng, who praised Xi Su's courage.

sentences.zh: 且慕化遠來，於義宜益不宜奪也。

translations.literal: Moreover admiring transformation from afar, in righteousness it is fitting to increase, not to strip away.
translations.idiomatic: Men who come from afar to submit should be rewarded, not robbed of their troops.

sentences.zh: 權善其言，還肅兵。

translations.literal: Quan thought well of his words and returned Su's troops.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan agreed and gave Xi Su his men back.

sentences.zh: 瑜使甘寧前據夷陵，曹仁分眾圍寧，寧困急，使使請救。

translations.literal: Yu sent Gan Ning forward to occupy Yiling; Cao Ren divided the host to besiege Ning; Ning was pressed in emergency and sent a messenger to beg rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu sent Gan Ning to Yiling; Cao Ren surrounded him; Gan Ning cried for help.

sentences.zh: 諸將以兵少不足分，蒙謂瑜、普曰：「留凌公績，蒙與君行，解圍釋急，勢亦不久，蒙保公績能十日守也。

translations.literal: The generals thought the troops too few to divide; Meng said to Yu and Pu, 'Leave Lord Ling Tong; Meng with you, sirs, will go—lifting the siege and releasing the emergency will also not be long; Meng guarantees Lord Ling can hold ten days.'
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng told Zhou Yu to leave Ling Tong holding the line while they relieved Gan Ning—ten days, he swore, Ling could hold.

sentences.zh: 」又說瑜分遣三百人柴斷險道，賊走可得其馬。

translations.literal: Again he persuaded Yu separately to dispatch three hundred men to cut firewood and block the perilous road—when bandits flee their horses can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: He urged three hundred men to block the escape route with felled timber and seize enemy horses.

sentences.zh: 瑜從之。

translations.literal: Yu followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu agreed.

sentences.zh: 軍到夷陵，即日交戰，所殺過半。

translations.literal: When the army reached Yiling, that day they joined battle; those killed were more than half.
translations.idiomatic: At Yiling they fought the same day and killed more than half the enemy.

sentences.zh: 敵夜遁去，行遇柴道，騎皆捨馬步走。

translations.literal: The enemy by night fled away; marching they met the blocked road; the cavalry all abandoned horses and went on foot.
translations.idiomatic: The foe fled by night, hit the barricade, and abandoned their horses.

sentences.zh: 兵追蹙擊，獲馬三百匹，方船載還。

translations.literal: Troops pursued, pressed, and struck; they obtained three hundred horses and returned with square-linked boats.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit took three hundred horses and ferried them home on linked boats.

sentences.zh: 於是將士形勢自倍，乃渡江立屯，與相攻擊，曹仁退走。

translations.literal: Thereupon officers and soldiers' situation doubled itself; then they crossed the river and set camp, mutually attacking; Cao Ren withdrew and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Morale doubled; they crossed the river, pressed Cao Ren, and drove him back.

sentences.zh: 遂據南郡，撫定荊州。

translations.literal: Thereupon they held Nan commandery and soothed and settled Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: They secured Nan commandery and pacified Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 還，拜偏將軍，領尋陽令。

translations.literal: Returning, he was appointed Lieutenant General, acting as magistrate of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: On return he became lieutenant general and acting magistrate of Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 魯肅代周瑜，當之陸口，過蒙屯下。

translations.literal: Lu Su replaced Zhou Yu; going to Lukou he passed below Meng's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su, replacing Zhou Yu en route to Lukou, passed Lü Meng's camp.

sentences.zh: 肅意尚輕蒙，或說肅曰：「呂將軍功名日顯，不可以故意待也，君宜顧之。

translations.literal: Su's intent still belittled Meng; someone said to Su, 'General Lü's merit and name grow daily manifest—one cannot treat him with old intent; you, sir, ought to visit him.'
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su still looked down on him until a friend urged a courtesy call.

sentences.zh: 」遂往詣蒙。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went to visit Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su went to see him.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，蒙問肅曰：「君受重任，與關羽為鄰，將何計畧以備不虞？

translations.literal: When wine was merry, Meng asked Su, 'You, sir, bear heavy responsibility and border Guan Yu—what stratagems will you prepare against the unforeseen?'
translations.idiomatic: Over wine Lü Meng asked how Lu Su meant to guard against Guan Yu.

sentences.zh: 」肅造次應曰：「臨時施宜。

translations.literal: Su hastily answered, 'When the time comes apply what fits.'
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su answered carelessly that he would improvise.

sentences.zh: 」蒙曰：「今東西雖為一家，而關羽實熊虎也，計安可不豫定？

translations.literal: Meng said, 'Now east and west though are one house, yet Guan Yu is in truth a bear and tiger—how can plans not be settled in advance?'
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng replied that allies or not, Guan Yu was a tiger—plans could not wait.

sentences.zh: 」因為肅畫五策。

translations.literal: Thereupon for Su he sketched five stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: He laid out five concrete plans for Lu Su.

sentences.zh: 肅於是越席就之，拊其背曰：「呂子明，吾不知卿才畧所及乃至於此也。

translations.literal: Su thereupon crossed the mat and drew near him, patted his back and said, 'Lü Ziming—I did not know your talent and strategy reached this far.'
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su crossed the room, clapped his back, and owned he had underestimated him.

sentences.zh: 」遂拜蒙母，結友而別。

translations.literal: Thereupon he bowed to Meng's mother, became friends, and parted.
translations.idiomatic: He paid respects to Lü Meng's mother and left as his sworn friend.

sentences.zh: 〈《江表傳》曰：初，權謂蒙及蔣欽曰：「卿今並當塗掌事，宜學問以自開益。

translations.literal: The Jiang biao zhuan states: At first Quan said to Meng and Jiang Qin, 'You now together are on the road holding affairs—it is fitting to study to open and enrich yourselves.'
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan told Lü Meng and Jiang Qin to study now that they held high office.

sentences.zh: 」蒙曰：「在軍中常苦多務，恐不容复讀書。

translations.literal: Meng said, 'In the army I always suffer many tasks—I fear there is no room again to read books.'
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng pleaded busy camp duty.

sentences.zh: 」權曰：「孤豈欲卿治經為博士邪？

translations.literal: Quan said, 'Does the orphan wish you, sir, to treat the classics and become a erudite?'
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan said he did not expect them to become textual doctors.

sentences.zh: 但當令涉獵見往事耳。

translations.literal: Only you ought to skim and see past affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He wanted them to read history for breadth.

sentences.zh: 卿言多務孰若孤，孤少時歷《詩》、《書》、《禮記》、《左傳》、《國語》，惟不讀《易》。

translations.literal: You speak of many tasks—who compares to the orphan? In youth I went through the Odes, Documents, Record of Rites, Zuo's Commentary, Guo yu—only I did not read the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: He listed his own reading as a busy ruler.

sentences.zh: 至統事以來，省三史、諸家兵書，自以為大有所益。

translations.literal: Down to taking charge of affairs I have examined the Three Histories and the various houses' military books—I consider myself greatly benefited.
translations.idiomatic: Since ruling he had read histories and military treatises to great profit.

sentences.zh: 如卿二人，意性朗悟，學必得之，寧當不為乎？

translations.literal: As for you two men's intent and nature bright and perceptive, study is sure to obtain it—how could you not do it?'
translations.idiomatic: Bright men like them could surely learn if they tried.

sentences.zh: 宜急讀《孫子》、《六韜》、《左傳》、《國語》及三史。

translations.literal: It is urgent to read Sunzi, Six Secret Teachings, Zuo's Commentary, Guo yu, and the Three Histories.
translations.idiomatic: He assigned Sunzi, Six Tao, Zuo, Guo yu, and the Three Histories.

sentences.zh: 孔子言『終日不食，終夜不寢以思，無益，不如學也』。

translations.literal: Confucius said, "All day not eating, all night not sleeping to think—there is no benefit; it is not as good as learning."'
translations.idiomatic: He quoted Confucius on learning versus empty thought.

sentences.zh: 光武當兵馬之務，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: Guangwu amid horse and army affairs did not release the scroll from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu read amid war.

sentences.zh: 孟德亦自謂老而好學。

translations.literal: Mengde also himself said old yet fond of learning.
translations.idiomatic: Even Cao Cao called himself an old book-lover.

sentences.zh: 卿何獨不自勉勗邪？

translations.literal: Why do you alone not exert yourselves?'
translations.idiomatic: Why should they not push themselves?

sentences.zh: 」蒙始就學，篤志不倦，其所覽見，舊儒不勝。

translations.literal: Meng thereupon undertook study, intent firm and unwearied; what he viewed and saw—old scholars could not surpass.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng studied relentlessly until he outshone pedants.

sentences.zh: 後魯肅上代周瑜，過蒙言議，常欲受屈。

translations.literal: Later when Lu Su went up replacing Zhou Yu, passing Meng's discussions, he always wished to be humbled.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Su succeeded Zhou Yu, Lü Meng's discourse often left him bested.

sentences.zh: 肅拊蒙背曰：「吾謂大弟但有武略耳，至於今者，學識英博，非復吳下阿蒙。

translations.literal: Su patted Meng's back and said, 'I thought you, great younger brother, had only martial strategy; as for now, learning and knowledge are heroically broad—you are no longer the A-Meng below Wu.'
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su said he was no longer the crude Lü Meng of old.

sentences.zh: 」蒙曰：「士別三日，即更刮目相待。

translations.literal: Meng said, 'When a gentleman parts three days, one should look again with fresh eyes.'
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng answered that three days change a man.

sentences.zh: 大兄今論，何一稱穰侯乎。

translations.literal: Great elder brother, today's discourse—why praise me like Lord Ranghou of Qin?
translations.idiomatic: He teased Lu Su for praising him like a famous minister of Qin.

sentences.zh: 兄今代公瑾，既難為繼，且與關羽為鄰。

translations.literal: Elder brother now replaces Gongjin—already hard to follow after; moreover you border Guan Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su had Zhou Yu's heavy shoes to fill and Guan Yu on his flank.

sentences.zh: 斯人長而好學，讀左傳略皆上口，梗亮有雄氣，然性頗自負，好陵人。

translations.literal: This man is grown and fond of learning; reading Zuo's Commentary he nearly all recites from memory; he is blunt and bright with heroic spirit, yet his nature is quite self-conceited and fond of overriding others.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu was well read, proud, and domineering.

sentences.zh: 今與為對，當有單衤復以

translations.literal: Now facing him as opponent, there ought to be single [text damaged: garment?] to
translations.idiomatic: Facing him you need a steady, single-minded stance—

translations.literal: (you)
translations.idiomatic: (the lacuna reads “you”)

sentences.zh: 待之。」。

translations.literal: treat him.".
translations.idiomatic: —and deal with him with deliberate patience.”

sentences.zh: 密為肅陳三策，肅敬受之，秘而不宣。

translations.literal: Secretly for Su he stated three stratagems; Su respectfully received them and kept them secret without proclaiming.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Lu Su three secret plans which Lu Su guarded closely.

sentences.zh: 權常歎曰：「人長而進益，如呂蒙、蔣欽，蓋不可及也。

translations.literal: Quan often sighed, saying, 'Men who grow and advance in benefit, like Lü Meng and Jiang Qin—probably cannot be overtaken.'
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan sighed that Lü Meng and Jiang Qin outgrew everyone.

sentences.zh: 富貴榮顯，更能折節好學，耽悅書傳，輕財尚義，所行可跡，並作國士，不亦休乎！」〉

translations.literal: Riches and honor, glory and display, yet able to bend measure and love study, delight in books and transmit, slight wealth and esteem righteousness—their conduct can be traced; together they became state knights—is it not fine!'〉
translations.idiomatic: Rich generals who still loved books and duty were true state pillars, he said.〉

sentences.zh: 時蒙與成當、宋定、徐顧屯次比近，三將死，子弟幼弱，權悉以兵並蒙。

translations.literal: At that time Meng together with Cheng Dang, Song Ding, and Xu Gu camped in neighboring stations; the three generals died, sons and younger brothers young and weak; Quan all with troops merged them to Meng.
translations.idiomatic: When three neighboring commanders died leaving young heirs, Sun Quan tried to merge their troops into Lü Meng's.

sentences.zh: 蒙固辭，陳啟顧等皆勤勞國事，子弟雖小，不可廢也。

translations.literal: Meng firmly declined, stating in memorial that Gu and the others all toiled for state affairs; though sons and younger brothers are small, they cannot be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng refused three times, arguing the orphans still deserved their fathers' commands.

sentences.zh: 書三上，權乃聽。

translations.literal: Three times he submitted writing; Quan thereupon listened.
translations.idiomatic: After three memorials Sun Quan yielded.

sentences.zh: 蒙於是又為擇師，使輔導之，其操心率如此。

translations.literal: Meng thereupon again for them chose teachers, had them tutor and guide—the care of his heart was always thus.
translations.idiomatic: He hired tutors for the young heirs himself.

sentences.zh: 魏使廬江謝奇為蘄春典農，屯皖田鄉，數為邊寇。

translations.literal: Wei sent Xie Qi of Lujiang as Qichun agricultural director, encamped at Wandian township, repeatedly becoming a border bandit.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's Xie Qi ran a military farm at Wan and raided the border.

sentences.zh: 蒙使人誘之，不從，則伺隙襲擊，奇遂縮退，其部伍孫子才、宋豪等，皆攜負老弱，詣蒙降。

translations.literal: Meng sent men to lure him; when he did not follow, then watched a gap and struck; Qi thereupon shrank back; his squads Sun Zicai, Song Hao, and others all carried old and weak on their backs and came to Meng to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng lured, ambushed, and broke him; his officers surrendered with families.

sentences.zh: 後從權拒曹公於濡須，數近奇計，又勸權夾水口立塢，所以備禦甚精，

translations.literal: Later following Quan in resisting Lord Cao at Ruxu, repeatedly offered near strange plans, again urged Quan to build ramparts pinching the water mouth—therefore the preparations and defense were extremely keen,
translations.idiomatic: At Ruxu he urged the twin ramparts across the narrows—defenses Cao Cao could not crack—

sentences.zh: 〈《吳錄》曰：權欲作塢，​​諸將皆曰：「上岸擊賊，洗足入船，何用塢為？

translations.literal: The Wu lu states: Quan wished to build the rampart; all the generals said, 'Going ashore to strike bandits, washing feet and entering the boat—what use is a rampart?'
translations.idiomatic: Generals mocked the idea of fortifying Ruxu—

sentences.zh: 」呂蒙曰：「兵有利鈍，戰無百勝，如有邂逅，敵步騎蹙人，不暇及水，其得入船乎？

translations.literal: Lü Meng said, 'Soldiers have sharp and dull; battle has no hundred victories—if there is a sudden encounter, enemy foot and horse press men—you will have no leisure to reach the water—can they get into the boat?'
translations.idiomatic: —Lü Meng warned that a reverse on land could trap men away from the boats.

sentences.zh: 」權曰：「善。

translations.literal: Quan said, 'Good.'
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan said, 'Good.'

sentences.zh: 」遂作之。〉

translations.literal: Thereupon he built it.〉
translations.idiomatic: They built the ramparts.〉

sentences.zh: 曹公不能下而退。

translations.literal: Lord Cao could not take it and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao could not force them and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 曹公遣朱光為廬江太守，屯皖，大開稻田，又令間人招誘鄱陽賊帥，使作內應。

translations.literal: Lord Cao sent Zhu Guang as Administrator of Lujiang, encamped at Wan, greatly opened paddy fields, and again ordered secret agents to entice and summon Poyang bandit chiefs to work as inner agents.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao planted Zhu Guang at Wan with irrigated fields and agents to stir Poyang bandits.

sentences.zh: 蒙曰：「皖田肥美，若一收孰，彼眾必增，如是數歲，操態見矣，宜早除之。

translations.literal: Meng said, 'Wan's fields are fertile and beautiful; if one harvest is gathered, their masses are sure to increase—thus for several years Cao's attitude will show; it is fitting to remove them early.'
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng warned that Wan's harvest would swell Cao's power and urged a strike.

sentences.zh: 」乃具陳其狀。

translations.literal: Thereupon he fully stated the situation.
translations.idiomatic: He laid out the intelligence in full.

sentences.zh: 於是權親征皖，引見諸將，問以計策。

translations.literal: Thereupon Quan personally campaigned against Wan, led in the generals, and asked stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan marched on Wan and polled his generals.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：諸將皆勸作土山，添攻具，蒙趨進曰：「治攻具及土山，必曆日乃成，城備既脩，外救必至，不可圖也。

translations.literal: The Wu shu states: All the generals urged building earthen hills and adding siege gear; Meng hurried forward and said, 'Making siege gear and earthen hills must take days to complete; once city defenses are repaired, outside rescue is sure to arrive—it cannot be planned.'
translations.idiomatic: The *Wu shu* records generals wanting slow siegework; Lü Meng argued speed.

sentences.zh: 且乘雨水以入，若留經日，水必向盡，還道艱難，蒙竊危之。

translations.literal: Moreover if we take advantage of rainy water to enter, if we stay passing days the water is sure to turn and run out—return road difficult—your servant privately fears this.
translations.idiomatic: He feared the rains would ebb and trap the army.

sentences.zh: 今觀此城，不能甚固，以三軍銳氣，四面並攻，不移時可拔，及水以歸，全勝之道也。

translations.literal: Now observing this city, it cannot be very firm—with the three armies' keen spirit, attack on four sides together, in no shifting time it can be taken; return by water while intact—this is the way of complete victory.'
translations.idiomatic: Storm the weak walls now with full fury and withdraw on high water—that wins cleanly.

sentences.zh: 」權從之。〉

translations.literal: Quan followed it.〉
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan agreed.〉

sentences.zh: 蒙乃薦甘寧為升城督，督攻在前，蒙以精銳繼之。

translations.literal: Meng thereupon recommended Gan Ning as colonel who raises the city, supervising attack in front; Meng with crack troops followed him.
translations.idiomatic: He put Gan Ning first in the escalade and followed with elites.

sentences.zh: 侵晨進攻，蒙手執枹鼓，士卒皆騰踴自升，食時破之。

translations.literal: At dawn they advanced the attack; Meng personally grasped the drum mallet and drum; soldiers all leaped and scrambled, climbing of themselves; at mealtime they broke it.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Lü Meng beat the drum himself; his men stormed the wall and took Wan by breakfast.

sentences.zh: 既而張遼至夾石，聞城已拔，乃退。

translations.literal: Afterward Zhang Liao reached Jiashi; hearing the city was already taken, then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liao arrived at Jiashi too late and turned back.

sentences.zh: 權嘉其功，即拜廬江太守，所得人馬皆分與之，別賜尋陽屯田六百戶，官屬三十人。

translations.literal: Quan praised his merit, immediately appointed Administrator of Lujiang, divided the obtained men and horses all to him, separately granted six hundred households of Xunyang military colony and thirty officials.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan made him governor of Lujiang, gave him the captured troops, six hundred colony households, and thirty staff.

sentences.zh: 蒙還尋陽，未期而盧陵賊起，諸將討擊不能禽，權曰：「鷙鳥累百，不如一鶚。

translations.literal: Meng returned to Xunyang; before the term was up bandits arose in Luling; the generals campaigned and struck but could not capture; Quan said, 'A hundred fierce birds are not as good as one osprey.'
translations.idiomatic: Before long Luling bandits baffled other generals; Sun Quan said one osprey beats a hundred kites.

sentences.zh: 」復令蒙討之。

translations.literal: Again he ordered Meng to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Lü Meng again.

sentences.zh: 蒙至，誅其首惡，餘皆釋放，復為平民。

translations.literal: When Meng arrived, he executed their chief evils; the rest all were released and again became commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng executed the ringleaders and freed the rest as farmers.

sentences.zh: 是時劉備令關羽鎮守，專有荊士，權命蒙西取長沙、零、桂三郡。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Bei ordered Guan Yu to guard and hold, monopolizing Jing soil; Quan ordered Meng west to take the three commanderies Changsha, Ling, and Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan ordered him west to seize Changsha, Lingling, and Guiyang from Guan Yu's grip.

sentences.zh: 蒙移書二郡，望風歸服，惟零陵太守郝普城守不降。

translations.literal: Meng sent letters to two commanderies; they submitted at the wind; only Lingling Administrator Hao Pu held the city guard and would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Two commanderies surrendered on his letter; only Hao Pu at Lingling held out.

sentences.zh: 而備自蜀親至公安，遣羽爭三郡。

translations.literal: Yet Bei himself came from Shu to Gong'an and sent Yu to contest the three commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei flew from Shu to Gong'an and sent Guan Yu to fight for them.

sentences.zh: 權時住陸口，使魯肅萬人屯益陽拒羽，而飛書召蒙，使捨零陵，急還助肅。

translations.literal: Quan at that time dwelt at Lukou, sent Lu Su with ten thousand men encamped at Yiyang to oppose Yu, and by flying letter summoned Meng, ordering him to abandon Lingling and hurry back to aid Su.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan at Lukou ordered Lu Su to block Guan Yu and recalled Lü Meng from Lingling.

sentences.zh: 初，蒙既定長沙，當之零陵，過酃，載南陽鄧玄之，玄之者郝普之舊也，欲令誘普。

translations.literal: At first, when Meng had already settled Changsha, going to Lingling, passing Ling he carried Deng Xuanzhi of Nanyang—Xuanzhi was Pu's old friend—and wished to have him entice Pu.
translations.idiomatic: He had picked up Deng Xuanzhi, Hao Pu's friend, to talk him down.

sentences.zh: 及被書當還，蒙秘之。

translations.literal: When he received the letter ordering return, Meng kept it secret.
translations.idiomatic: When the recall order came, Lü Meng hid it from Hao Pu.

sentences.zh: 夜召諸將，授以方畧，晨當攻城。

translations.literal: By night he summoned the generals, handed them stratagems; at dawn they ought to attack the city.
translations.idiomatic: He briefed his officers for a dawn assault.

sentences.zh: 顧謂玄之曰：

translations.literal: He turned and said to Xuanzhi:
translations.idiomatic: He turned to Deng Xuanzhi and said,

sentences.zh: 郝子太聞世間有忠義事，亦欲為之，而不知時也。

translations.literal: Master Hao Zitai has heard there are loyal and righteous deeds in the world and also wishes to do them, yet does not know the times.
translations.idiomatic: He told Deng to tell Hao Pu that loyalty must fit the moment.

sentences.zh: 左將軍在漢中，為夏侯淵所圍。

translations.literal: The General of the Left is in Hanzhong, besieged by Xiahou Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He lied that Liu Bei was trapped in Hanzhong by Xiahou Yuan.

sentences.zh: 關羽在南郡，今至尊身自臨之。

translations.literal: Guan Yu is in Nan commandery; now the Exalted One personally comes against him.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed Sun Quan himself was moving on Guan Yu in Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 近者破樊本屯，救酃，逆為孫規所破。

translations.literal: Recently he broke Fan's main camp, went to save Ling, but heading east was broken by Sun Gui.
translations.idiomatic: He invented a defeat—Fan camp broken, relief to Ling crushed by Sun Gui.

sentences.zh: 此皆目前之事，君所親見也。

translations.literal: These are all matters before your eyes that you, sir, personally have seen.
translations.idiomatic: All this, he said, Hao Pu could verify with his own eyes.

sentences.zh: 彼方首尾倒懸，救死不給，豈有餘力復營此哉？

translations.literal: They are just then head and tail inverted, saving death without surplus—how can they have surplus strength again to manage this?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei's side was stretched to breaking—no help would reach Lingling.

sentences.zh: 今吾士卒精銳，人思致命。

translations.literal: Now our soldiers and officers are keen and fine; every man thinks to give his life.
translations.idiomatic: Wu's host was fresh and eager to die for the cause.

sentences.zh: 至尊遣兵，相繼於道。

translations.literal: The Exalted One sends troops one after another on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan's reinforcements were already marching down the road.

sentences.zh: 今子太以旦夕之命，待不可望之救。

translations.literal: Now Zitai with the life of a morning and evening awaits rescue that cannot be hoped for.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Pu clung to a day-to-day existence while hoping for help that would never come.

sentences.zh: 猶牛蹄中魚，冀賴江漢，其不可恃亦明矣。

translations.literal: Like a fish in an ox's hoofprint hoping in the Jiang and Han—it is clear this cannot be relied on.
translations.idiomatic: He was a fish in a hoofprint dreaming of the great rivers—no hope there.

sentences.zh: 若子太必能一士卒之心，保孤城之守，尚能稽延旦夕，以待所歸者，可也。

translations.literal: If Zitai is sure able to unify the soldiers' hearts and preserve lone-city defense, still able to prolong morning and evening to await those who would return—that can be done.
translations.idiomatic: If he could truly hold the garrison together and buy time for relief, that would be one thing.

sentences.zh: 今吾計力度慮，而以攻此，曾不移日，而城必破，城破之後，身死何益於事，而令百歲老母，戴白受誅，豈不痛哉？

translations.literal: Now I reckon strength and measure plans and use them to attack this—in no shifting day the city is sure to be broken; after the city is broken, what benefit to the affair is dying in body, and causing a hundred-year-old mother with white hair to suffer execution—is it not painful?
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng swore the city would fall in hours; dying then would only doom his aged mother to execution.

sentences.zh: 度此家不得外問，謂援可恃，故至於此耳。

translations.literal: I reckon this house gets no outside news, thinks rescue can be relied on—therefore it has reached this ear.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Pu was cut off from news and mistook rumors for hope.

sentences.zh: 君可見之，為陳禍福。

translations.literal: You, sir, can see him and for him set forth disaster and blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Xuanzhi should show him the truth.

sentences.zh: 玄之見普，具宣蒙意，普懼而聽之。

translations.literal: When Xuanzhi saw Pu, he fully proclaimed Meng's intent; Pu feared and obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Xuanzhi delivered Lü Meng's ultimatum; Hao Pu yielded in terror.

sentences.zh: 玄之先出報蒙：「普尋後當至。

translations.literal: Xuanzhi first went out to report to Meng, 'Pu presently afterward will arrive.'
translations.idiomatic: Deng ran ahead to say Hao Pu was coming.

sentences.zh: 」蒙豫敕四將，各選百人，普出，便入守城門。

translations.literal: Meng beforehand ordered four generals, each to select a hundred men—when Pu comes out, then enter and guard the city gates.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng set four hundred men to seize the gates the moment Hao Pu stepped out.

sentences.zh: 須臾普出，蒙迎執其手，與俱下船。

translations.literal: In a moment Pu came out; Meng welcomed and grasped his hand and with him went down to the boat.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Pu emerged; Lü Meng took his hand and led him aboard.

sentences.zh: 語畢，出書示之。

translations.literal: When speech was finished, he produced the letter and showed it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Then he showed Sun Quan's recall order.

sentences.zh: 因拊手大笑。

translations.literal: Thereupon he clapped hands and laughed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng laughed and clapped.

sentences.zh: 普見書，知備在公安，而羽在益陽，慚恨入地。

translations.literal: When Pu saw the letter, he knew Bei was at Gong'an and Yu at Yiyang—shame and hatred entered the earth.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Pu saw he had been lied to—Liu Bei at Gong'an, Guan Yu at Yiyang—and burned with shame.

sentences.zh: 蒙留

translations.literal: Meng left Sun He
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng left Sun He

sentences.zh: （孫河）

translations.literal: (Sun He)
translations.idiomatic: (Sun He)

sentences.zh: ，委以後事，即日引軍赴益陽。

translations.literal: , entrusted him with rear affairs; that day he led the army hastening to Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: to handle rear business while he himself led the main column to Yiyang that same day.

sentences.zh: 劉備請盟，權乃歸普等。

translations.literal: Liu Bei requested alliance; Quan thereupon returned Pu and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei sued for peace; Sun Quan returned Hao Pu and company.

sentences.zh: 割湘水，以零陵還之。

translations.literal: They cut at the Xiang River and returned Lingling to him.
translations.idiomatic: They split at the Xiang and restored Lingling to Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 以尋陽、陽新為蒙奉邑。

translations.literal: They made Xunyang and Yangxin Meng's fief income.
translations.idiomatic: Xunyang and Yangxin became Lü Meng's revenue fiefs.

sentences.zh: 師還，遂徵合肥，既撤兵，為張遼等所襲，蒙與淩統以死扦衛。

translations.literal: When the army returned, then they campaigned against Hefei; already having withdrawn troops, they were struck by Zhang Liao and others; Meng together with Ling Tong with death barred and defended.
translations.idiomatic: On the retreat from Hefei, Zhang Liao ambushed them; Lü Meng and Ling Tong fought a rearguard to the death.

sentences.zh: 後曹公又大出濡須，權以蒙為督，據前所立塢，置強弩萬張於其上，以拒曹公。

translations.literal: Later when Lord Cao again came out greatly to Ruxu, Quan made Meng supervisor, holding the ramparts built before, setting ten thousand strong crossbows on them to resist Lord Cao.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao returned to Ruxu, Lü Meng commanded the old ramparts with massed crossbows.

sentences.zh: 曹公前鋒屯未就，蒙攻破之，曹公引退。

translations.literal: Lord Cao's van encampment was not yet finished; Meng broke and defeated it; Lord Cao led withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: He smashed Cao's unfinished forward camp and drove him back.

sentences.zh: 拜蒙左護軍、虎威將軍。

translations.literal: He appointed Meng Left Protector of the Army, General Who Shows Tiger Might.
translations.idiomatic: He was named left protector of the army and general who shows tiger might.

sentences.zh: 魯肅卒，蒙西屯陸口，肅軍人馬萬餘盡以屬蒙。

translations.literal: When Lu Su died, Meng encamped west at Lukou; Su's army men and horses more than ten thousand all were assigned to Meng.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Su died, Lü Meng took his ten thousand men at Lukou.

sentences.zh: 又拜漢昌太守，食下雋、劉陽、漢昌、州陵。

translations.literal: Again he was appointed Administrator of Hanchang, feeding on Xiajun, Liuyang, Hanchang, and Zhouling.
translations.idiomatic: He became governor of Hanchang with revenue from four counties.

sentences.zh: 與關羽分土接境，知羽驍雄，有並兼心，且居國上流，其勢難久。

translations.literal: Bordering Guan Yu's divided soil, he knew Yu was fierce and heroic, had a mind to annex and merge, and dwelt upstream of the state—its situation could not long endure.
translations.idiomatic: He faced Guan Yu upstream, a conqueror by nature who could not be a lasting neighbor.

sentences.zh: 初，魯肅等以為曹公尚存，禍難始構，宜相輔協，與之同仇，不可失也。

translations.literal: At first Lu Su and others thought Lord Cao still survived, disaster and hardship just beginning—it was fitting mutually to assist and cooperate, sharing hatred with him; it could not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su's party had wanted to keep Liu's alliance while Cao Cao lived.

sentences.zh: 蒙乃密陳計策曰：「今令徵虜守南郡，潘璋住白帝，蔣欽將遊兵萬人循江上下，應敵所在，蒙為國家前據襄陽，如此，何憂於操，何賴於羽？

translations.literal: Meng thereupon secretly stated stratagem, saying, 'Now order the Campaign General to guard Nan commandery, Pan Zhang to dwell at Baidicheng, Jiang Qin to lead roaming troops ten thousand along the river up and down, answering wherever the enemy is; Meng for the state will advance to hold Xiangyang—thus what worry of Cao, what reliance on Yu?'
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng laid out a full redeployment—Sun Huan at Nan commandery, Pan Zhang at Baidi, Jiang Qin mobile on the river, himself at Xiangyang—to end fear of both north and Guan Yu.

sentences.zh: 且羽君臣，矜其詐力，所在反覆，不可以腹心待也。

translations.literal: Moreover Yu lord and ministers pride themselves on deceitful force; wherever they are they turn back and forth—they cannot be treated as heart and belly.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei's court traded on treachery and could never be trusted as kin.

sentences.zh: 今羽所以未便東向者，以至尊聖明，蒙等尚存也。

translations.literal: The reason Yu has not yet conveniently turned east is because the Exalted One is sagely bright and Meng and others still survive.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu had not struck east only because Sun Quan and Lü Meng still lived.

sentences.zh: 今不於強壯時圖之，一日僵僕，欲復陳力，其可得邪？

translations.literal: Now if we do not plan him in his strong years, one day he falls stiff—wishing again to display strength, how can it be obtained?'
translations.idiomatic: Strike him in his prime, he urged, or never again.

sentences.zh: 」權深納其策，又聊復與論取徐州意。

translations.literal: Quan deeply took in his plan, again casually again with him discussed the intent to take Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan embraced the plan and chatted about Xu Province too.

sentences.zh: 蒙對曰：「今操遠在河北，新破諸袁，撫集幽、冀，未暇東顧。

translations.literal: Meng answered, saying, 'Now Cao is far in Hebei, newly broken the various Yuans, soothing and gathering You and Ji—not leisure to look east.'
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng said Cao Cao was busy pacifying the north.

sentences.zh: 徐土守兵，聞不足言，往自可克。

translations.literal: Xu Province's guarding troops, hearing, are not worth speaking of—going of itself can overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Xu's garrison was weak on paper.

sentences.zh: 然地勢陸通，驍騎所聘，至尊今日得徐州，操後旬必來爭，雖以七八萬人守之，猶當懷憂。

translations.literal: Yet the terrain communicates by land; fine cavalry gallop there—if the Exalted One today obtains Xu Province, Cao within ten days afterward is sure to come contest it; though with seventy or eighty thousand men guarding it, still one ought to harbor worry.
translations.idiomatic: But Xu was open country—Cao Cao would retake it at once even with a huge garrison.

sentences.zh: 不如取羽，全據長江，形勢益張。

translations.literal: Better take Yu and fully hold the Long River—the situation grows more spreading.'
translations.idiomatic: Better seize Guan Yu and own the whole Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 」權尤以此言為當。

translations.literal: Quan especially thought this speech right.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan judged that the wiser move.

sentences.zh: 及蒙代肅，初至陸口，外倍修恩厚，與羽結好。

translations.literal: When Meng replaced Su, on first arrival at Lukou outwardly doubly cultivated kindness and thickness, befriending Yu in good faith.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Meng replaced Lu Su at Lukou he showered Guan Yu with false friendship.

sentences.zh: 後羽討樊，留兵將備公安、南郡。

translations.literal: Later when Yu campaigned against Fan, he left troops and generals to prepare Gong'an and Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Guan Yu marched on Fan he left rear guards at Gong'an and Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 蒙上疏曰：「羽討樊而多留備兵，必恐蒙圖其後故也。

translations.literal: Meng submitted a memorial saying, 'Yu campaigns against Fan yet leaves many rear-guard troops—surely because he fears Meng plotting his rear.'
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng told Sun Quan that Guan Yu's heavy rear guard showed fear of a Wu stab in the back.

sentences.zh: 蒙常有病，乞分士眾還建業，以治疾為名。

translations.literal: Meng constantly has illness; I beg to divide troops and masses returning to Jianye, in the name of treating illness.
translations.idiomatic: He feigned serious illness and asked to return to the capital for cure.

sentences.zh: 羽聞之，必撤備兵，盡赴襄陽。

translations.literal: When Yu hears it, he is sure to withdraw rear-guard troops, all hastening to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu would strip the rear to reinforce Fan.

sentences.zh: 大軍浮江，晝夜馳上，襲其空虛，則南郡可下，而羽可擒也。

translations.literal: The great host floating the river, day and night galloping upstream, striking their emptiness—then Nan commandery can be taken and Yu can be captured.'
translations.idiomatic: Wu could then sail upstream, strike the empty forts, and bag Guan Yu.

sentences.zh: 」遂稱病篤，權乃露檄召蒙還，陰與圖計。

translations.literal: Thereupon he claimed grave illness; Quan then openly issued summons recalling Meng, secretly plotting with him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan published an open recall for the supposedly dying Lü Meng while plotting in secret.

sentences.zh: 羽果信之，稍撤兵以赴樊。

translations.literal: Yu indeed believed it, gradually withdrew troops to hasten to Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu swallowed the bait and thinned his rear.

sentences.zh: 魏使於禁救樊，羽盡擒禁等，人馬數萬，託以糧乏，擅取湘關米。

translations.literal: Wei sent Yu Jin to rescue Fan; Yu captured Jin and the whole host, men and horses numbering in the tens of thousands; claiming grain shortage he on his own authority took rice at the Xiang barrier.
translations.idiomatic: When Guan Yu captured Yu Jin's host he seized Wu's grain at the Xiang tax barrier for supply.

sentences.zh: 權聞之，遂行。

translations.literal: When Quan heard it, he thereupon set out.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan marched at the news.

sentences.zh: 先遣蒙在前。

translations.literal: First he sent Meng in front.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng led the van.

sentences.zh: 蒙至尋陽，盡伏其精兵𦩷𦪇中，使白衣搖櫓，作商賈人服，晝夜兼行，至羽所置江邊屯候，盡收縛之，是故羽不聞知。

translations.literal: When Meng reached Xunyang, he fully hid his crack troops inside decked barges, had men in white shake the oars, wear merchant trader clothes, travel day and night, reaching Yu's riverbank watch posts set in place—seized and bound them all—therefore Yu did not hear or know.
translations.idiomatic: At Xunyang he hid soldiers in merchant hulls in white, seized every river picket, and Guan Yu heard nothing.

sentences.zh: 遂到南郡，士仁、麋芳皆降。

translations.literal: Thereupon they reached Nan commandery—Shiren and Mi Fang both submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Shiren and Mi Fang surrendered Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：將軍士仁在公安拒守，蒙令虞翻說之。

translations.literal: The Wu shu states: General Shiren held Gong'an in defense; Meng ordered Yu Fan to persuade him.
translations.idiomatic: The *Wu shu* tells how Yu Fan talked down Shiren at Gong'an.

sentences.zh: 翻至城門，謂守者曰：「吾欲與汝將軍語。

translations.literal: When Fan reached the city gate, he said to the defenders, 'I wish to speak with your general.'
translations.idiomatic: Yu Fan asked the gate guards for Shiren.

sentences.zh: 」仁不肯相見。

translations.literal: Ren was unwilling to meet.
translations.idiomatic: Shiren refused to see him.

sentences.zh: 乃為書曰：「明者防禍於未萌，智者圖患於將來，知得知失，可與為人，知存知亡，足別吉凶。

translations.literal: Then he wrote a letter saying, 'The wise guard disaster before it sprouts; the wise plan trouble before it comes; knowing gain and knowing loss, one can with him be a man; knowing survival and knowing destruction, enough to distinguish auspicious and inauspicious.'
translations.idiomatic: Yu Fan's letter argued foresight and survival.

sentences.zh: 大軍之行，斥候不及施，烽火不及舉，此非天命，必有內應。

translations.literal: The great army's march—outposts had no time to deploy, beacon fires no time to raise—this is not Heaven's mandate; there must be inner agents.
translations.idiomatic: Wu had struck too fast for beacons—someone inside must have turned.

sentences.zh: 將軍不先見時，時至又不應之，獨守縈帶之城而不降，死戰則毀宗滅祀，為天下譏笑。

translations.literal: The General does not foresee the time; when the time comes again does not respond—alone guarding a belt-wound city yet not submitting—if you die fighting then ancestral temple is destroyed and sacrifice cut off, mocked and laughed at by the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Resistance would destroy Shiren's clan and win only mockery.

sentences.zh: 呂虎威欲徑到南郡，斷絕陸道，生路一塞，案其地形，將軍為在箕舌上耳，奔走不得免，降則失義，竊為將軍不安，幸熟思焉。

translations.literal: General Lü Huwei wishes to go straight to Nan commandery, cut off the land road—when one road of life is blocked, pressing the terrain, the General is on the tongue of a winnowing basket—running cannot escape; to submit loses righteousness—for your servant privately the General is not secure; happily think it through carefully.'
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng could seal the roads and leave Shiren trapped like grain on a winnow—Yu Fan begged him to think.

sentences.zh: 」仁得書，流涕而降。

translations.literal: When Ren obtained the letter, he wept and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Shiren wept and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 翻謂蒙曰：「此譎兵也，當將仁行，留兵備城。

translations.literal: Fan said to Meng, 'This is deceitful troops—one ought to lead Ren along and leave troops to prepare the city.'
translations.idiomatic: Yu Fan warned it might be a ruse—escort Shiren under guard.

sentences.zh: 」遂將仁至南郡。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led Ren to Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: They brought Shiren south under escort.

sentences.zh: 南郡太守麋芳城守，蒙以仁示之，遂降。

translations.literal: Nan commandery Administrator Mi Fang guarded the city; Meng showed Ren to him; thereupon he submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Fang surrendered when he saw the captured Shiren.

sentences.zh: 《吳錄》曰：初，南郡城中失火，頗焚燒軍器。

translations.literal: The Wu lu states: At first in Nan commandery city fire broke out and rather burned military gear.
translations.idiomatic: The *Wu lu* adds that a fire in Nan commandery had destroyed stores.

sentences.zh: 羽以責芳，芳內畏懼，權聞而誘之，芳潛相和。

translations.literal: Yu blamed Fang; Fang inwardly feared; Quan heard and enticed him; Fang secretly allied.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu had rebuked Mi Fang; Sun Quan won him secretly.

sentences.zh: 及蒙攻之，乃以牛酒出降。〉

translations.literal: When Meng attacked him, then with oxen and wine he came out to submit.〉
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Meng attacked, Mi Fang came out with wine and cattle to yield.〉

sentences.zh: 蒙入據城，盡得羽及將士家屬，皆撫慰，約令軍中不得乾歷人家，有所求取。

translations.literal: Meng entered and held the city, fully obtained Yu's and officers' and soldiers' families, all soothed and comforted, ordering the army not to violate or pass through people's houses or take what they sought.
