translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng seized the city, comforted Guan Yu's dependents, and forbade looting.

sentences.zh: 蒙麾下士，是汝南人，取民家一笠，以覆官鎧，官鎧雖公，蒙猶以為犯軍令，不可以鄉里故而廢法，遂垂涕斬之。

translations.literal: A soldier under Meng's command, a man of Runan, took one rain hat from a commoner's house to cover official armor—though official armor was public property, Meng still considered it violation of military law; one could not because of fellow-town reason abolish the law—thereupon weeping he beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: He executed a hometown soldier for borrowing a villager's hat to shield state armor.

sentences.zh: 於是軍中震慄，道不拾遺。

translations.literal: Thereupon in the army they trembled with fear; on the road nothing was picked up if dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The camp went rigid—lost goods lay untouched.

sentences.zh: 蒙旦暮使親近存卹耆老，問所不足，疾病者給醫藥，饑寒者賜衣糧。

translations.literal: Meng morning and evening sent intimates to inquire after and comfort the old; asked what they lacked; to the sick he gave medicine; to the hungry and cold he granted clothes and grain.
translations.idiomatic: He fed the elderly, healed the sick, clothed the hungry.

sentences.zh: 羽府藏財寶，皆封閉以待權至。

translations.literal: Yu storehouse treasures and goods were all sealed to await Quan's arrival.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu's treasury he sealed for Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 羽還，在道路，數使人與蒙相聞，蒙輒厚遇其使，周遊城中，家家致問，或手書示信。

translations.literal: When Yu returned on the road, repeatedly he sent men to communicate with Meng; Meng always thickly treated his messengers, toured the city, to every household conveyed inquiries, or by hand wrote letters showing trust.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu's envoys Lü Meng feasted and sent home with letters proving families safe.

sentences.zh: 羽人還，私相參訊，咸知家門無恙，見待過於平時，故羽吏士無鬬心。

translations.literal: When Yu's men returned, privately they asked one another—all knew their gates were unharmed, treatment exceeding the usual—therefore Yu's clerks and soldiers had no will to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu's army learned their families were safer than before and lost the will to fight.

sentences.zh: 會權尋至，羽自知孤窮，乃走麥城，西至漳鄉，眾皆委羽而降。

translations.literal: It happened that Quan soon arrived; Yu himself knew isolation and poverty, then fled to Maicheng, west reaching Zhang township—the host all cast off Yu and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan closed in; Guan Yu fled to Maicheng and his men deserted.

sentences.zh: 權使朱然、潘璋斷其徑路，即父子俱獲，荊州遂定。

translations.literal: Quan ordered Zhu Ran and Pan Zhang to cut off his paths—father and son were both captured together; Jing Province thereupon was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ran and Pan Zhang cut his retreat; father and son were taken and Jingzhou fell.

sentences.zh: 以蒙為南郡太守，封孱陵候，

translations.literal: He made Meng Administrator of Nan commandery, enfeoffed him Marquis of Chanling,
translations.idiomatic: He named Lü Meng governor of Nan commandery and marquis of Chanling—

sentences.zh: 〈《江表傳》曰：權於公安大會，呂蒙以疾辭，權笑曰：「禽羽之功，子明謀也，今大功已捷，慶賞未行，豈邑邑邪？

translations.literal: The Jiang biao zhuan states: Quan at Gong'an held a great assembly; Lü Meng declined on grounds of illness; Quan laughed and said, 'The merit of capturing Yu was Ziming's plan; now the great merit is already achieved, rewards and feasts not yet carried out—are you sulky?'
translations.idiomatic: The *Jiangbiao zhuan* says Lü Meng skipped the victory feast until Sun Quan coaxed him.

sentences.zh: 」乃增給步騎鼓吹，敕選虎威將軍官屬，並南郡、廬江二郡威儀。

translations.literal: Thereupon he increased foot and horse military music, ordered selection of tiger-general staff, together with Nan commandery and Lujiang two commanderies' ceremonial guard.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan added guards of honor, musicians, and full staff for a tiger general across two commanderies.

sentences.zh: 拜畢還營，兵馬導從，前後鼓吹，光燿於路。〉

translations.literal: When appointment was finished returning to camp, horse and army led before and behind with military music, splendor shining on the road.〉
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng returned to camp in full pomp.〉

sentences.zh: 賜錢一億，黃金五百斤。

translations.literal: He was given cash one hundred million, gold five hundred jin.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan paid him a hundred million cash and five hundred jin of gold.

sentences.zh: 蒙固辭金錢，權不許。

translations.literal: Meng firmly declined gold and cash; Quan did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng refused the treasure; Sun Quan would not hear it.

sentences.zh: 封爵未下。

translations.literal: The enfeoffment rank had not yet descended.
translations.idiomatic: The formal patent had not yet arrived.

sentences.zh: 會蒙疾發，權時在公安，迎置內殿。

translations.literal: It happened that Meng's illness broke out; Quan at that time was at Gong'an, welcomed and placed him in the inner hall.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng fell ill at Gong'an; Sun Quan brought him into the palace.

sentences.zh: 所以治護者萬方，募封內有能愈蒙疾者，賜千金。

translations.literal: The means used to treat and nurse were in ten thousand ways; he ordered that within the sealed domain whoever could cure Meng's illness would be given a thousand jin of gold.
translations.idiomatic: He offered a thousand jin for a cure.

sentences.zh: 時有針加，權為之慘戚，欲數見其顏色，又恐勞動，常穿壁瞻之，見小能下食則喜，顧左右言笑，不然則咄唶，夜不能寐。

translations.literal: At times when needles were applied, Quan for it was miserable and grieved, wished repeatedly to see his complexion, again feared tiring him, often bored a hole in the wall to look at him—when he saw he could slightly eat then was pleased, looked to left and right speaking and laughing; if not then he sighed with vexation, at night could not sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan watched through a wall, rejoiced at every bite of food, and lay sleepless when Lü Meng failed.

sentences.zh: 病中瘳，為下赦令，群臣畢賀。

translations.literal: In illness he improved; for him he issued an amnesty order; the host of ministers all congratulated.
translations.idiomatic: A brief rally brought a general amnesty and court rejoicing.

sentences.zh: 後更增篤，權自臨視，命道士於星辰下為之請命。

translations.literal: Later it turned graver again; Quan personally came to look, ordered a Daoist under the stars to for him beg life.
translations.idiomatic: When he worsened Sun Quan attended him and had Daoists pray under the stars.

sentences.zh: 年四十二，遂卒於內殿。

translations.literal: At age forty-two, thereupon he died in the inner hall.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the inner hall at forty-two.

sentences.zh: 時權哀痛甚，為之降損。

translations.literal: At that time Quan mourned extremely and for him lowered and reduced [mourning display].
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan mourned him with exceptional rites.

sentences.zh: 蒙未死時，所得金寶諸賜盡付府藏，敕主者命絕之日皆上還，喪事務約。

translations.literal: Before Meng died, the obtained gold and treasures and various gifts he fully delivered to the treasury store, ordering the steward that on the day life ends all should be sent up; funeral affairs were kept simple.
translations.idiomatic: Before death he returned every gift to the treasury and asked a plain funeral.

sentences.zh: 權聞之，益以悲感。

translations.literal: When Quan heard it, he all the more was moved with grief.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan wept the more for that humility.

sentences.zh: 蒙少不修書傳，每陳大事，常口占為箋疏。

translations.literal: In youth Meng did not cultivate letters and transmission; whenever he stated great affairs, he always orally composed memorials and notes.
translations.idiomatic: Young Lü Meng had dictated his state papers to scribes.

sentences.zh: 常以部曲事為江夏太守蔡遺所白，蒙無恨意。

translations.literal: He constantly because of headquarters affairs was impeached by Administrator of Jiangxia Cai Yi; Meng had no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yi once impeached him over troop affairs; Lü Meng bore no grudge.

sentences.zh: 及豫章太守顧邵卒，權問所用，蒙因薦遺奉職佳吏，權笑曰：「君欲為祁奚耶？

translations.literal: When Administrator of Yuzhang Gu Shao died, Quan asked whom to use; Meng thereupon recommended Yi as a fine clerk holding office; Quan laughed and said, 'Do you, sir, wish to be Qi Xi?'
translations.idiomatic: When a post opened he recommended his old critic Cai Yi—Sun Quan compared him to the noble Qi Xi.

sentences.zh: 」於是用之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he employed him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan hired Cai Yi.

sentences.zh: 甘寧粗暴好殺，既常失蒙意，又時違權令，權怒之，蒙輒陳請：「天下未定，鬥將如寧難得，宜容忍之。

translations.literal: Gan Ning was rough and violent, fond of killing—already he often missed Meng's intent, and again at times disobeyed Quan's orders; Quan was angry with him; Meng always stated requesting, 'Under heaven not yet settled, brawling generals like Ning are hard to obtain—it is fitting to tolerate him.'
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan raged at Gan Ning, Lü Meng begged patience for so rare a fighter.

sentences.zh: 」權遂厚寧，卒得其用。

translations.literal: Quan thereupon treated Ning thickly and in the end obtained his use.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan indulged Gan Ning and reaped his service.

sentences.zh: 蒙子霸襲爵，與守塚三百家，復田五十頃。

translations.literal: Meng's son Ba inherited the rank, with three hundred households guarding the tomb, again fifty qing of field restored.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lü Ba inherited the title with three hundred tomb guards and fifty qing of land.

sentences.zh: 霸卒，兄琮襲候。

translations.literal: When Ba died, elder brother Cong inherited the marquis.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Ba died, his brother Lü Cong took the marquisate.

sentences.zh: 琮卒，弟睦嗣。

translations.literal: When Cong died, younger brother Mu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Cong died, Lü Mu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 孫權與陸遜論周瑜、魯肅及蒙曰：

translations.literal: Sun Quan with Lu Xun discussed Zhou Yu, Lu Su, and Meng, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan said to Lu Xun of Zhou Yu, Lu Su, and Lü Meng—

sentences.zh: 公瑾雄烈，膽略兼人，遂破孟德，開拓荊州，邈焉難繼，君今繼之。

translations.literal: Gongjin was fierce and bold, courage and strategy surpassing others—thereupon he broke Mengde, opened and expanded Jing Province—far away hard to follow; you, sir, now succeed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu was a blazing strategist who broke Cao Cao and carved out Jingzhou—a standard almost impossible to match; you now walk in his footsteps.

sentences.zh: 公瑾昔要子敬來東，致達於孤，孤與宴語，便及大略帝王之業，此一快也。

translations.literal: Formerly Gongjin asked Zijing to come east, conveyed him to the orphan; the orphan feasted and conversed with him, and then reached the great outline of the emperor-king's enterprise—this was one joy.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Yu brought Lu Su east and introduced him, our first banquet already ranged the great theme of empire—that was my first delight in him.

sentences.zh: 後孟德因獲劉琮之勢，張言方率數十萬眾水步俱下。

translations.literal: Later Mengde by obtaining Liu Cong's momentum openly declared he would lead several hundred thousand water and foot troops down together.
translations.idiomatic: Then Cao Cao rode Liu Cong's surrender and boasted of a half-million host marching downriver.

sentences.zh: 孤普請諸將，諮問所宜，無適先對，至子佈、文表，俱言宜遣使修檄迎之，子敬即駁言不可，勸孤急呼公瑾，付任以眾，逆而擊之，此二快也。

translations.literal: The orphan generally summoned the generals and asked what was fitting; none was first to answer—down to Zibu and Wenbiao, both said it was fitting to send envoys to polish a proclamation and welcome him; Zijing immediately refuted that it could not be done, urged the orphan urgently to summon Gongjin, entrust him with the host, and go meet and strike them—this was a second joy.
translations.idiomatic: I polled my commanders; Zhang Zhao and Qin Song would have welcomed Cao Cao—until Lu Su alone said no and made me recall Zhou Yu for the battle. That was my second joy.

sentences.zh: 且其決計策意，出張、蘇遠矣。

translations.literal: Moreover his resolved planning and intent went far beyond Zhang and Su.
translations.idiomatic: His strategic clarity towered above the Zhang Zhao faction and the other waverers.

sentences.zh: 後雖勸吾借玄德地，是其一短，不足以損其二長也。

translations.literal: Later although he urged the orphan to lend land to Xuande—that was one shortcoming, not enough to harm his two long points.
translations.idiomatic: His later advice to cede ground to Liu Bei was a flaw—but it cannotcels his two great services.

sentences.zh: 周公不求備於一人，故孤忘其短而貴其長，常以比方鄧禹也。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou did not seek completeness in a single man—therefore the orphan forgot his shortcoming and prized his long points, often comparing him to Deng Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Like the Duke of Zhou, I do not demand perfection; I forgave that lapse and honored his strengths, and often compared him to Deng Yu of Han.

sentences.zh: 又子明少時，孤謂不辭劇易，果敢有膽而已。

translations.literal: Again Ziming in his youth—the orphan thought him only one who did not shun hard or easy, decisive and daring with courage—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Young Lü Meng I took for a mere daredevil who feared no odds.

sentences.zh: 及身長大，學問開益，籌略奇至，可以次於公瑾，但言議英發不及之耳。

translations.literal: When his body had grown and learning opened and enriched him, stratagem and planning reached the marvelous—he can rank next to Gongjin, only in fluent debate he does not reach him.
translations.idiomatic: Grown and lettered, his plans rivaled Zhou Yu's—second only in eloquence on the tongue.

sentences.zh: 圖取關羽，勝於子敬。

translations.literal: Plotting to take Guan Yu—he surpassed Zijing.
translations.idiomatic: In the design to capture Guan Yu he outdid Lu Su.

sentences.zh: 子敬答孤書云：『帝王之起，皆有驅除，羽不足忌。

translations.literal: Zijing answered the orphan's letter saying, 'The rise of emperor-kings always has driving-off; Guan Yu is not worth fearing.'
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su once wrote that every founding age sweeps rivals aside and that Guan Yu was nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 』此子敬內不能辦，外為大言耳，孤亦恕，不苟責也。

translations.literal: That was Zijing unable within yet grand words without—the orphan also forgave him and did not harshly blame.
translations.idiomatic: That was bluster masking doubt—I indulged him and did not press the point.

sentences.zh: 然其作軍屯營，不失令行禁止，部界無廢負，路無拾遺，其法亦美也。

translations.literal: Yet when he made army camps and garrisons, he did not miss making orders obeyed and prohibitions enforced; within his borders there was no waste or burden; on the roads nothing picked up if dropped—his methods too were fine.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his camps ran tight—orders absolute, districts orderly, not a coin taken from the road. That discipline was itself a gift.

translations.literal: 【Appraisal】
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal

sentences.zh: 評曰：曹公乘漢相之資，挾天子而掃群桀，新蕩荊城，仗威東夏，於時議者莫不疑貳。

translations.literal: The appraisal states: Lord Cao riding the resources of Han chancellor, clasping the Son of Heaven to sweep the host of heroes, freshly shaking Jing city, leaning on awe in the eastern summer—at that time debaters none did not doubt and hesitate.
translations.idiomatic: The historian's verdict: Cao Cao as chancellor, holding the emperor, sweeping the lords, fresh from crushing Jingzhou and thundering at the east—left every counselor wavering.

sentences.zh: 周瑜、魯肅建獨斷之明出眾人之表，實奇才也。

translations.literal: Zhou Yu and Lu Su established the brightness of solitary decision, rising above the multitude's surface—they were truly extraordinary talents.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu and Lu Su alone saw the clear course and stood above the panic—true prodigies.

sentences.zh: 呂蒙勇而有謀，斷識軍計，譎郝普，禽關羽，最其妙者。

translations.literal: Lü Meng was brave yet had stratagem, cut and knew military plans, deceived Hao Pu, captured Guan Yu—the most marvelous of these.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng combined courage with guile—tricking Hao Pu, caging Guan Yu—the peak of his art.

sentences.zh: 初雖輕果妄殺，終於克己，有國士之量，豈徒武將而已乎！

translations.literal: At first though light and rash and killed recklessly, in the end he was able to master himself—he had the capacity of a state knight; how was he merely a martial general!
translations.idiomatic: He began as a rash killer but ended in self-mastery—worthy of the title state knight, not a mere brawler.

sentences.zh: 孫權之論，優劣允當，故載錄焉。

translations.literal: Sun Quan's discourse on their good and ill was balanced and fitting—therefore it is recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan's judgments on the three ring true, so the text preserves them here.
